name: Bitcoin Mainnet: Correctness of the Consensus Rules
description:
## Why verify the mainnet consensus rules

Bitcoin nodes must agree on which blocks are valid and on the spendable outputs that a valid block creates. A discrepancy in an arithmetic boundary, script operation, or historical exception can change that decision. This mission targets **all Bitcoin mainnet consensus rules**, including their historical applicability, through a source-linked Lean 4 development. BIP68 relative sequence locks are the first component, not the completion criterion.

The implementation reference is Bitcoin Core revision `a773e1e33b349dc819b5a0edc1c7a4839dc73b48`, with unmodified mainnet parameters. Freezing the revision makes the target reviewable; future protocol changes require an explicit scope revision. Historical coverage means the pinned implementation's treatment of blocks at historical heights, including exceptions. Reproducing every obsolete software release is a separate question. [Validation source](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/a773e1e33b349dc819b5a0edc1c7a4839dc73b48/src/validation.cpp), [mainnet parameters](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/a773e1e33b349dc819b5a0edc1c7a4839dc73b48/src/kernel/chainparams.cpp).

The specification developed over multiple generations: the original proof-of-work chain design, later script and duplicate-transaction rules, relative locks, witness transactions, and Taproot. These layers remain relevant together. Existing Lean work on absolute transaction lock time provides a potential reusable starting point; it does not discharge relative locks or whole-system correctness. [Original design](https://bitcoin.org/bitcoin.pdf), [BIP68](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/100ba872c808946155b1eeb8c4568058f2eea0a7/bip-0068.mediawiki), [existing lock-time formalization](https://github.com/ProofOfKeags/btc-verified/blob/2fdeb40ca2b3f289896ed14a3340ad231cd16538/BtcVerified/Consensus/LockTime.lean).

## Blocks, histories, and validation outcomes

A **chain state** contains a validated ancestor history and a **UTXO set**, the outputs currently available to spend, including their values, scripts, creation heights, and coinbase status. A candidate block contains a header and an ordered transaction list. An explicit time input represents the local clock used when checking a newly received header. A **consensus specification** states validity and state transitions independently of the translated implementation.

The executable model must cover the complete validation path. Calling `ConnectBlock` alone is insufficient: header and contextual checks occur elsewhere. The full-validation setting enables proof-of-work, commitment, and script checks; assumed-valid shortcuts are not evidence of those checks. Temporary future-time failures must remain distinguishable from permanent invalidity. [Validation entry points and caller contracts](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/a773e1e33b349dc819b5a0edc1c7a4839dc73b48/src/validation.cpp).

## Whole-consensus target and component milestones

Write $R(S)$ for independently specified reachability from mainnet genesis, $C(S,B,t)$ for the source-linked validation outcome, and $V(S,B,t)$ for declarative admissibility at the supplied time. The intended acceptance theorem is

$$\forall S,B,t,\quad R(S)\Longrightarrow
\bigl(C(S,B,t)\text{ accepts}\iff V(S,B,t)\bigr).$$

For every accepted block, the implementation and specification must also agree on the resulting ledger state:

$$C(S,B,t)=\operatorname{Accept}(S')
\Longrightarrow S'=\operatorname{ApplySpec}(S,B).$$

The target additionally requires correct genesis initialization, interpretation of serialized data, historical rule selection, and state restoration across disconnect/reconnect operations. The candidate block is not assumed valid. A classification contract must account for time-dependent rejection without permanently invalidating an otherwise eligible header.

These formulas are the **goal contract to formalize**, not existing Lean declarations. A complete concrete definition of the history, specification, executable validation pipeline, and state correspondence must precede the overarching theorem. The main theorem is `BitcoinBlock.acceptance` of component mission 13, the formalization of the acceptance contract above, to be selected once that mission is published; `BitcoinBlock.apply_spec` is the state-transition contract. Selecting the BIP68 theorem as the main theorem would incorrectly allow a partial result to complete this mission.

The component program covers:

1. Data representation, serialization, hashes, finite-width arithmetic, and source coverage.
2. **BIP68**, including sequence decoding, threshold accumulation, output heights, bounds, and the caller bridge.
3. Transaction structure, duplicate inputs, amount ranges, UTXO availability, maturity, fees, subsidy, and coinbase rewards.
4. Absolute lock time, median-time-past calculation and selection, and script-level lock checks.
5. Header validity, compact targets, proof of work, retargeting, and cumulative work.
6. Block structure, Merkle mutation detection, witness commitments, weight, and signature-operation limits.
7. Legacy Script and P2SH, signature encodings, signature hashes, and exact ECDSA verification behavior.
8. SegWit version-zero execution and signing rules, Taproot, Schnorr verification, and Tapscript.
9. Historical flags, activation boundaries, genesis behavior, and named block exceptions.
10. Full validation composition, ledger updates, reorganization correctness, and closure of the source-coverage audit.

### Ledger-safety corollaries

The overarching equivalence and state-transition theorems must yield the following named results, each stated as its own milestone once the ledger model exists:

1. **No value creation by a transaction.** An accepted ordinary transaction consumes available outputs, leaves unrelated outputs unchanged, and does not increase total ledger value.
2. **Block value bound.** An accepted block increases total ledger value by at most its subsidy; fees only move value between outputs.
3. **Issuance bound.** Repeated valid extensions from genesis keep cumulative issuance below 21 million BTC, accounting for the subsidy schedule, unclaimed coinbase value, unspendable outputs, output-key overwrites, and the historical duplicate-coinbase exceptions.

### Reuse and modeling notes

Existing Lean work in [btc-verified](https://github.com/ProofOfKeags/btc-verified) documents proofs for serialization, Merkle properties, UTXO accounting, and transaction checks, and lists BIP68 relative locks and full block composition as outstanding. Those modules are candidates for reuse after their representations and assumptions are audited against the pinned revision; their documentation has not been independently built or audited here. [Documented coverage](https://github.com/ProofOfKeags/btc-verified/blob/master/BtcVerified/Consensus/README.md)

The BIP68 model uses natural-number subtraction, so $h-1$ truncates to $0$ and matches the source's $\max(h-1,0)$. The sequence-seconds mask-and-shift stays below $2^{25}$ and cannot overflow a 32-bit word. Real chains have monotone median-time-past; the component theorems deliberately do not assume it, so they hold for the weaker model.

Concrete hash and signature-verification semantics are required for the final result on purpose: functional correctness needs them, while cryptographic hardness and unforgeability are separate projects with computational assumptions. Because the full scope is large, the BIP68 component, UTXO accounting, and the Merkle and serialization layers are each suitable as an independently reviewable sub-mission feeding this umbrella goal.

The BIP68 component is published as its own mission, *BIP68 Relative Lock-Time: Bitcoin Core Sequence Locks Agree with the Specification*, whose two definitions and five open theorems are referenced here rather than re-declared. Its four supporting statements are component milestones of this mission; its goal theorem `BitcoinBIP68.core_correct` is a component result, not this mission's goal. The other areas are roadmap obligations pending concrete formalization, not already linked theorem milestones.

### Component missions

The roadmap areas are being delivered as separately reviewable missions whose published theorems this mission references:

1. **BIP68 relative lock-time** — goal `BitcoinBIP68.core_correct` (proved): the Core sequence-lock helpers decide exactly the BIP68 condition. Area 2.
2. **Block subsidy and the 21 million bound** — goal `BitcoinSubsidy.issuance_bound`: cumulative `GetBlockSubsidy` stays below `MAX_MONEY` at every height. Area 3 (issuance).
3. **Proof of work: compact targets and retargeting** — goal `BitcoinPow.nextWork_permitted`: `CalculateNextWorkRequired` always passes `PermittedDifficultyTransition`, with exact characterizations of `SetCompact`/`GetCompact` overflow and rounding. Area 5.
4. **Merkle root and the CVE-2012-2459 mutation check** — goal `BitcoinMerkle.dup_block`: duplicating an aligned trailing block of $2^k$ leaves preserves the root and is detected. Area 6 (Merkle).
5. **UTXO accounting and the ledger supply bound** — goal `BitcoinUtxo.ledger_bound`: from an empty ledger, accepted blocks (with `CheckTransaction`, BIP30, `CheckTxInputs`, fee accumulation and the coinbase bound) hold at most the summed subsidies; with milestones `tx_conservation` (no value creation) and `block_bound`. Area 3 (accounting) and the three ledger-safety corollaries above.
6. **Block headers: median time past and the contextual rules** — goal `BitcoinHeader.mtp_mono_chain`: along any chain obeying `time-too-old`, the median time past is non-decreasing; with the characterization of `ContextualCheckBlockHeader` and the BIP34/66/65 version floors. Area 4 (median-time-past) and the header part of area 5.
7. **Soft-fork activation: script flags by height** — goal `BitcoinActivation.flags_mono`: `GetBlockScriptFlags` is monotone in height for ordinary blocks, with the activation order, the two hash-keyed exception blocks, and the CSV lock-time flag. Area 9 (historical flags and named exceptions).
8. **Script: `CScriptNum`, the legacy interpreter, and the P2PKH template** — goal `BitcoinScript.p2pkh_correct`: against the transcribed `EvalScript` (full non-push opcode table of `SigVersion::BASE`, element/operation/stack limits, disabled opcodes) and `VerifyScript` for plain output scripts, `DUP HASH160 <h> EQUALVERIFY CHECKSIG` succeeds exactly when the key hashes to $h$ and the signature verifies, for every oracle; with the `CScriptNum` round-trip and minimality, the `CastToBool` characterization, the CVE-2010-5137 rule and the 201-operation limit. Area 7 (legacy Script), with hashes, signature checking and lock-time checks as oracle parameters.
9. **Serialization, CompactSize, SHA-256d/Hash160, weights, the genesis block** — goal `BitcoinSer.block_roundtrip`: the block, transaction and header encodings round-trip for well-formed values, with concrete SHA-256 and RIPEMD-160, the CompactSize canonical form, `GetSerializeSize`-based weights, and the genesis hash and merkle root by kernel evaluation. Area 1.
10. **Signatures: strict DER, sighash (legacy and BIP143), secp256k1 ECDSA and BIP340 Schnorr, concrete P2PKH** — goal `BitcoinSig.derEncode_complete`: `IsValidSignatureEncoding` accepts exactly the canonical encodings, with the exact `SignatureHash` quirks (`SIGHASH_SINGLE` bug, `FindAndDelete`), the field and group arithmetic of secp256k1, and the Script mission's P2PKH theorem instantiated with the real checker. Area 7 (signatures) and part of area 8 (BIP143).
11. **VerifyScript: P2SH, native and wrapped SegWit v0, unknown witness versions** — goal `BitcoinVerify.p2wpkh_correct`: the dispatch of `VerifyScript`/`VerifyWitnessProgram`/`ExecuteWitnessScript`, with the four spending templates characterized two-directionally and the malleability and upgrade rules as universal statements. Area 8 (SegWit v0) and BIP16.
12. **Taproot: key path, script-path commitment, BIP341 sighash, Tapscript rules** — goal `BitcoinTaproot.keypath_correct`: the version-1 branch, the tagged hashes, the merkle path, the tweak check, `SignatureHashSchnorr`, `CheckSchnorrSignature`, and the BIP342 interpreter rules, closing the script layer with no parameter left. Area 8 (Taproot, Schnorr, Tapscript).
13. **Block validation composed** — goal `BitcoinBlock.acceptance`: the executable validation path `C(S, B, t)` (`AcceptBlockHeader`, `CheckBlock`, `ContextualCheckBlock`, `ConnectBlock`, with `GetBlockScriptFlags`, BIP30 history, `IsBIP30Repeat`, undo data) composed from the component missions' functions, the declarative `V(S, B, t)` and `ApplySpec(S, B)`, and the proofs of **`R(S) ⟹ (C accepts ⟺ V)`** and **`C = Accept(S') ⟹ S' = ApplySpec(S, B)`**, together with the exact classification of temporary future-time rejections, the well-formedness of reachable states, strictly increasing chain work, and `DisconnectBlock` restoring the ledger. Area 10 and the remaining parts of area 9 (genesis, BIP30 exceptions). Its goal theorem is the intended main theorem of this mission once published.

Each is parametric where the layer below is not yet formalized (an abstract hash type for Merkle, an abstract subsidy function for the ledger bound, abstract transaction ids, an oracle for the hash, signature and lock-time primitives of Script), so that composing them is a matter of instantiation. Missions 9–13 perform that instantiation: the composition in mission 13 uses the concrete hashes, signatures, scripts, subsidy, difficulty, median time, activation flags and BIP68 functions of the published missions, with no parameter left abstract. Two technical notes for solvers of the remaining areas: the platform rejects proofs that use `bv_decide`, because its certificate relies on `Lean.ofReduceBool`; bit-level facts must be proved through `BitVec.toNat` and the `Nat` bitwise lemmas. And the BIP68 equivalence `core_correct` holds without its admissibility and overflow hypotheses, since Lean's integers are unbounded; those hypotheses are what the separate bounds theorem needs to justify the fixed-width reading of the source.

## What completion would establish

Completion would give kernel-checked acceptance and state-transition results for a concrete Lean rendering of the pinned mainnet validation rules. Both acceptance of valid candidates and rejection of invalid candidates matter. The source-to-Lean correspondence must be documented and independently reviewed; a proof about manually transcribed Lean code alone is not a proof about a compiled Bitcoin Core binary.

The current BIP68 statements have independent read-backs and compiled locally with intentional open proof placeholders. Previous differential checks exercised 2,014 cases against extracted Core helper bodies. Those checks provide evidence about that component only; they neither prove its universal theorems nor validate the broader mission. No whole-consensus correctness proof is claimed.

Existing Formalpedia definitions and proofs should be reused after their assumptions and representations have been checked. Generic Merkle-tree or signature results cannot be treated as Bitcoin-specific theorems without a correspondence result.

## Why composition and historical behavior are difficult

Local helper contracts leave premises for callers to establish. For BIP68, these include input heights, ancestor clocks, activation flags, coinbase exclusion, and arithmetic bounds. Completing the helper proof does not establish those premises for block validation.

Historical behavior is not captured by a single table of activation heights. The pinned implementation contains script-flag exceptions indexed by block hash and special duplicate-coinbase handling. Its genesis transaction is not connected to the spendable ledger. These cases must be represented explicitly. [Flag selection, connection, and disconnection](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/a773e1e33b349dc819b5a0edc1c7a4839dc73b48/src/validation.cpp).

Script correctness also depends on execution version, exact byte encodings, signature-message construction, and rules for unknown or reserved features. Mempool policy flags must not accidentally become consensus requirements. [Script interpreter](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/a773e1e33b349dc819b5a0edc1c7a4839dc73b48/src/script/interpreter.cpp).

## Formalization scope and completion criteria

All mainnet consensus branches reachable under the fixed parameters are in scope, across historical heights and admissible alternative histories. This includes formerly external BIP68 caller responsibilities. The top-level result must discharge component premises or expose a genuine source limitation; assuming successful validation, defining the specification by calling the implementation, or leaving unimplemented rules behind always-true predicates is unacceptable.

The full development must supply concrete hash and signature-verification semantics. Conditional intermediate lemmas are welcome, but unresolved crypto-verification or script oracles do not satisfy the final goal. Functional correctness does not require proving cryptographic hardness. Machine bounds must be justified; cases that reveal undefined source arithmetic are findings, not cases to hide through convenient hypotheses.

The core target uses full validation from genesis. Equivalence of caches or optional validation shortcuts requires separate justification if incorporated. Networking, wallet behavior, relay policy, miner incentives, and compiler correctness are outside this consensus-rule target. Cumulative-work comparison and valid reorganization are included; universal agreement on arrival-order tie-breaking is not asserted.

Completion requires the concrete global theorem, all necessary component proofs without proof holes or custom correctness axioms, historical boundary coverage, source correspondence review, and a branch-level inventory with no unexplained consensus omissions. The roadmap is an initial decomposition, not a claim that the source inventory is already exhaustive. The comprehensive goal must be formalized and audited before this proposal is ready for submission.

## Selected references

- Satoshi Nakamoto. *Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System*, 2008. [Paper](https://bitcoin.org/bitcoin.pdf).
- Bitcoin Core contributors. *Bitcoin Core mainnet validation implementation*, pinned revision reviewed 2026. [Source](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/tree/a773e1e33b349dc819b5a0edc1c7a4839dc73b48/src).
- Mark Friedenbach, BtcDrak, Nicolas Dorier, and kinoshitajona. *BIP68: Relative lock-time using consensus-enforced sequence numbers*, Bitcoin Improvement Proposals, 2015. [Specification](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/100ba872c808946155b1eeb8c4568058f2eea0a7/bip-0068.mediawiki).
- Bitcoin Improvement Proposal authors. *Consensus specifications and their historical context*, collection at revision `100ba872c808946155b1eeb8c4568058f2eea0a7`. [Collection](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/tree/100ba872c808946155b1eeb8c4568058f2eea0a7).
- ProofOfKeags contributors. *btc-verified: Absolute transaction lock time*, pinned revision reviewed 2026. [Lean development](https://github.com/ProofOfKeags/btc-verified/blob/2fdeb40ca2b3f289896ed14a3340ad231cd16538/BtcVerified/Consensus/LockTime.lean).

items.theorem_title: BIP68 input data, declarative eligibility, and arithmetic domain
items.natural_language_statement:
An input consists of an unsigned 32-bit sequence word $s$ and a natural-number coin height $c$. A context consists of a natural-number candidate height $H$ and a total function $M:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ supplying median times. Put $h^-=\max(h-1,0)$, $d=s\bmod 65536$, and let $D$ and $T$ be the tests for bits 31 and 22, expressed by quotient and remainder. Enforcement $E$ means that the unsigned version is at least two and the flags value is odd. A single input satisfies its delay when

$$D\ \lor\ \begin{cases}M(c^-)+512d\le M(H^-),&T,\\ c+d\le H,&\neg T.\end{cases}$$

The transaction-level predicate holds when $E$ is false or every input satisfies that condition. The expected output height list replaces an input height by zero exactly when $E$ and $D$ both hold, preserving order and repetitions.

The admissible-context predicate requires $0<H\le2^{31}-1$, every input height at most $H$, and $M(h)\le2^{63}-1$ for all $h\le H$. A separate no-overflow predicate requires the selected pre-subtraction sum to be at most $2^{31}-1$ for an enforced height input, or $2^{63}-1$ for an enforced time input. It imposes no sum condition on disabled inputs or when enforcement is off. Heights and clocks are nonnegative by type; no clock monotonicity is assumed. Empty input lists are included. The records alone impose no validity conditions: the predicates supply them when a theorem needs them.

These definitions separate per-input eligibility from the implementation's threshold-accumulation algorithm. Decidable instances are supplied for the three flag predicates.
items.definition:
import Std

namespace BitcoinBIP68

structure Input where
  sequence : BitVec 32
  coinHeight : Nat
  deriving Repr, DecidableEq

structure Context where
  height : Nat
  mtp : Nat → Nat

def int32Max : Nat := 2147483647
def int64Max : Nat := 9223372036854775807

def specEnabled (version flags : BitVec 32) : Prop :=
  2 ≤ version.toNat ∧ flags.toNat % 2 = 1

def specDisabled (sequence : BitVec 32) : Prop :=
  sequence.toNat / 2147483648 = 1

def specTimeBased (sequence : BitVec 32) : Prop :=
  (sequence.toNat / 4194304) % 2 = 1

def specDelay (sequence : BitVec 32) : Nat :=
  sequence.toNat % 65536

instance (version flags : BitVec 32) : Decidable (specEnabled version flags) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (2 ≤ version.toNat ∧ flags.toNat % 2 = 1))

instance (sequence : BitVec 32) : Decidable (specDisabled sequence) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (sequence.toNat / 2147483648 = 1))

instance (sequence : BitVec 32) : Decidable (specTimeBased sequence) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable ((sequence.toNat / 4194304) % 2 = 1))

def inputSatisfied (ctx : Context) (input : Input) : Prop :=
  specDisabled input.sequence ∨
    if specTimeBased input.sequence then
      ctx.mtp (input.coinHeight - 1) + 512 * specDelay input.sequence ≤
        ctx.mtp (ctx.height - 1)
    else
      input.coinHeight + specDelay input.sequence ≤ ctx.height

def satisfiesBIP68 (version flags : BitVec 32) (ctx : Context)
    (inputs : List Input) : Prop :=
  ¬ specEnabled version flags ∨ ∀ input ∈ inputs, inputSatisfied ctx input

def expectedHeights (version flags : BitVec 32) (inputs : List Input) : List Nat :=
  inputs.map fun input =>
    if specEnabled version flags ∧ specDisabled input.sequence then 0
    else input.coinHeight

def admissible (ctx : Context) (inputs : List Input) : Prop :=
  0 < ctx.height ∧ ctx.height ≤ int32Max ∧
  (∀ h, h ≤ ctx.height → ctx.mtp h ≤ int64Max) ∧
  ∀ input ∈ inputs, input.coinHeight ≤ ctx.height

def noOverflow (version flags : BitVec 32) (ctx : Context)
    (inputs : List Input) : Prop :=
  ∀ input ∈ inputs, specEnabled version flags → ¬ specDisabled input.sequence →
    if specTimeBased input.sequence then
      ctx.mtp (input.coinHeight - 1) + 512 * specDelay input.sequence ≤ int64Max
    else
      input.coinHeight + specDelay input.sequence ≤ int32Max

end BitcoinBIP68

items.readback:
**`Input`.** An input is a record consisting of a sequence value represented by a 32-bit vector and a coin height that is a natural number. The unsigned integer represented by the sequence can be any integer from $0$ through $2^{32}-1$, inclusive; the coin height can be any natural number, including $0$, with no bound or relationship to the sequence imposed. The declaration also supplies a printable representation and decidable equality for these records.

**`Context`.** A context is a record consisting of a height $H$ that is a natural number and a total function $M:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$. The height may be $0$, and the function has a natural-number value at every natural-number argument. This declaration imposes no bound, monotonicity, or other relationship on the height or the function.

**`int32Max`.** This natural-number constant is defined to be $2{,}147{,}483{,}647$.

**`int64Max`.** This natural-number constant is defined to be $9{,}223{,}372{,}036{,}854{,}775{,}807$.

**`specEnabled`.** For any two 32-bit vectors called version and flags, let $v$ and $f$ be their unsigned integer values, each between $0$ and $2^{32}-1$, inclusive. The proposition defined here holds exactly when $2\le v$ and the remainder of $f$ on division by $2$ is $1$. Thus the comparison uses the unsigned value of the version, and there are no further restrictions on either vector.

**`specDisabled`.** For any 32-bit sequence vector with unsigned integer value $s\in\{0,\ldots,2^{32}-1\}$, the proposition defined here holds exactly when the integer quotient of $s$ by $2{,}147{,}483{,}648$ is $1$. Equivalently, it holds exactly for $2^{31}\le s\le 2^{32}-1$; no condition is imposed on the lower 31 bits.

**`specTimeBased`.** For any 32-bit sequence vector with unsigned integer value $s\in\{0,\ldots,2^{32}-1\}$, the proposition defined here holds exactly when the remainder modulo $2$ of the integer quotient of $s$ by $4{,}194{,}304$ is $1$. Equivalently, bit 22, with the least significant bit numbered 0, is set; the other bits are unrestricted, including bit 31.

**`specDelay`.** For any 32-bit sequence vector with unsigned integer value $s\in\{0,\ldots,2^{32}-1\}$, this function returns the natural number $s\bmod 65{,}536$. Its value therefore ranges from $0$ through $65{,}535$, inclusive, and is unaffected by any of the upper 16 bits.

**Decidability instance for `specEnabled`.** For every version vector and flags vector, both of width 32 bits, this declaration supplies a decision of the proposition $2\le v\;\land\;f\bmod 2=1$, where $v$ and $f$ are the corresponding unsigned integer values. The decision contains either a proof that both conditions hold or a proof that their conjunction does not hold; it does not assert that the conjunction is true for all vectors.

**Decidability instance for `specDisabled`.** For every 32-bit sequence vector with unsigned integer value $s$, this declaration supplies a decision of the proposition $\lfloor s/2{,}147{,}483{,}648\rfloor=1$. The decision contains either a proof of this equality or a proof that it is false, including all sequence values from $0$ through $2^{32}-1$.

**Decidability instance for `specTimeBased`.** For every 32-bit sequence vector with unsigned integer value $s$, this declaration supplies a decision of the proposition $\lfloor s/4{,}194{,}304\rfloor\bmod 2=1$. The decision contains either a proof of this equality or a proof that it is false, with no restriction on the remaining bits of the sequence.

**`inputSatisfied`.** Given any context consisting of a natural-number height $H$ and a total function $M:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$, and any input consisting of a 32-bit sequence with unsigned value $s$ and a natural-number coin height $c$, write $d=s\bmod 65{,}536$. The defined proposition holds exactly when either $\lfloor s/2{,}147{,}483{,}648\rfloor=1$, or the following selected inequality holds: if $\lfloor s/4{,}194{,}304\rfloor\bmod 2=1$, the inequality is $M(\max(c-1,0))+512d\le M(\max(H-1,0))$; otherwise it is $c+d\le H$. These are non-strict inequalities in natural-number arithmetic, with no overflow or wrapping. In particular, subtraction of $1$ from $0$ yields $0$, a zero delay is allowed, and the first alternative makes the proposition true regardless of the selected inequality. There is no assumption that $H$ is positive, that $c\le H$, or that $M$ is bounded or monotone.

**`satisfiesBIP68`.** Given arbitrary 32-bit version and flags vectors with unsigned values $v$ and $f$, any context with natural-number height $H$ and total function $M:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$, and any finite list of inputs, the defined proposition holds exactly when either $2\le v\;\land\;f\bmod 2=1$ is false, or every input in the list meets the following condition. For that input's unsigned sequence value $s$ and natural-number coin height $c$, either $\lfloor s/2{,}147{,}483{,}648\rfloor=1$, or, writing $d=s\bmod65{,}536$, the inequality $M(\max(c-1,0))+512d\le M(\max(H-1,0))$ holds when $\lfloor s/4{,}194{,}304\rfloor\bmod2=1$, and $c+d\le H$ holds otherwise. All additions and multiplications are in the unbounded natural numbers and the displayed maxima express subtraction truncated at zero. The empty list makes the universal condition true, and failure of the version-and-flags conjunction makes the entire proposition true for any list. No bound or positivity condition on heights, no bound on the sums, and no monotonicity condition on $M$ is included.

**`expectedHeights`.** Given arbitrary 32-bit version and flags vectors with unsigned values $v$ and $f$ and any finite list of inputs, this function returns a list of natural numbers of the same length and in the same order. For each input with unsigned 32-bit sequence value $s$ and natural-number coin height $c$, the corresponding output is chosen to be $0$ when both $2\le v\;\land\;f\bmod2=1$ and $\lfloor s/2{,}147{,}483{,}648\rfloor=1$ hold; otherwise that output is $c$. An empty input list returns an empty list. Repeated inputs remain repeated, coin heights may already be $0$, and failure of the version-and-flags conjunction causes every coin height to be copied as given.

**`admissible`.** Given any context with natural-number height $H$ and total function $M:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ and any finite list of inputs, the defined proposition holds exactly when all four requirements hold: $0<H$; $H\le2{,}147{,}483{,}647$; for every natural number $h$, the implication $h\le H\Rightarrow M(h)\le9{,}223{,}372{,}036{,}854{,}775{,}807$ holds; and every input in the list has coin height at most $H$. The function bound includes $h=0$ and $h=H$, and imposes no condition at arguments greater than $H$. Coin heights may be $0$, input sequences are unrestricted, and no monotonicity of $M$ or bound on a delay-added sum is required. An empty list makes only the requirement on input coin heights vacuous; the three context requirements still apply.

items.natural_language_statement:
The implementation reads unsigned 32-bit words using the masks $2^{31}$, $2^{22}$, and $65535$, and converts the masked delay to seconds with a nine-bit left shift. Enforcement checks unsigned version at least two and flags bit zero.

An accumulator consists of integer thresholds $a,b$ and a reversed height list. It starts at $(-1,-1,[])$. Processing a disabled input prepends zero and leaves both thresholds unchanged. For an enabled time input it updates $b$ to $\max(b,M(\max(c-1,0))+512d-1)$; for an enabled height input it updates $a$ to $\max(a,c+d-1)$. Both enabled branches prepend the original coin height. The masked delay and seconds are computed with bit-vector operations. The final subtraction takes place in the integers, preserving the $-1$ sentinel.

If transaction-level enforcement is off, calculation preserves all original heights and returns thresholds $(-1,-1)$. The output height list is obtained by reversing the accumulator's list. Evaluation accepts precisely when

$$a<H\quad\land\quad b<M(\max(H-1,0)).$$

The sequence-lock function composes calculation with evaluation. These are total functions over the model's records; their definitions do not assume valid histories or bounded arithmetic. The main theorem states the domain appropriate for comparison with Core. This is a manual transcription of the named routines, not a formal C++ semantics or a proof about compiled machine code.

# Def_BIP68_Core read-back

**`coreEnabled`.** For any two 32-bit bit vectors called version and flags, this Boolean is true exactly when the unsigned natural-number value of version is at least $2$ and the bitwise AND of flags with $1$ is nonzero. Thus version ranges over all unsigned values from $0$ through $2^{32}-1$, and only the least significant bit of flags affects this result; versions $0$ and $1$ give false regardless of flags.

**`coreDisabled`.** For any 32-bit bit vector called sequence, this Boolean is true exactly when its bitwise AND with hexadecimal $80000000$, namely $2^{31}$, is nonzero. Equivalently, bit $31$, counting the least significant bit as bit $0$, is set; all other bits are ignored.

**`coreTimeBased`.** For any 32-bit bit vector called sequence, this Boolean is true exactly when its bitwise AND with hexadecimal $00400000$, namely $2^{22}$, is nonzero. Equivalently, bit $22$, counting the least significant bit as bit $0$, is set; all other bits, including bit $31$, are ignored.

**`coreDelay`.** For any 32-bit bit vector called sequence, this natural number is the unsigned value of the bitwise AND of sequence with hexadecimal $0000ffff$, namely $65535$. It is the unsigned value of the lowest sixteen bits, lies between $0$ and $65535$ inclusive, and is unaffected by every higher bit.

**`coreSeconds`.** For any 32-bit bit vector called sequence, this natural number is obtained by masking sequence with hexadecimal $0000ffff$, shifting the resulting 32-bit bit vector left by $9$ positions, and taking its unsigned value. If $d$ is the unsigned value of the lowest sixteen bits of sequence, the result is $512d$; because $0 ≤ d ≤ 65535$, this shift loses no nonzero bit and its result ranges from $0$ to $33553920$ inclusive in multiples of $512$. Every higher bit of the original sequence is ignored.

**`Accumulator`.** An accumulator consists of two unrestricted integers, named `minHeight` and `minTime`, together with a finite list of natural numbers named `heightsRev`. There are no conditions relating these fields, no bounds or sign restrictions on the integer fields, and no restriction on the list, which may be empty. A printable representation and a decision procedure for equality of accumulators are generated from these fields.

**`initial`.** This particular accumulator has integer `minHeight` equal to $-1$, integer `minTime` equal to $-1$, and `heightsRev` equal to the empty list.

**`coreStep`.** Given a context consisting of a natural-number height and an arbitrary function $M$ from natural numbers to natural numbers, an accumulator with integer fields $H,T$ and natural-number list $R$, and an input consisting of a 32-bit sequence and a natural-number coin height $c$, this function returns an accumulator as follows. If sequence bit $31$ is set, the result is $(H,T,0::R)$, where $x::R$ denotes prepending $x$ to $R$. Otherwise, let $d$ be the unsigned value of the lowest sixteen sequence bits: if sequence bit $22$ is set, the result is $(H,\max(T,M(\max(c-1,0))+512d-1),c::R)$; if bit $22$ is unset, it is $(\max(H,c+d-1),T,c::R)$. The expressions added to $H$ or $T$ are computed in the integers after converting the natural-number quantities, so their final subtraction of $1$ may produce $-1$; the subtraction in the argument to $M$ is natural-number subtraction, so $c=0$ uses $M(0)$. The context height is not used by this function. Inputs with both bits $31$ and $22$ set take the first branch, and no bounds, monotonicity, or consistency assumptions are imposed on the context, input, or accumulator.

**`calculate`.** Given arbitrary 32-bit version and flags, a context consisting of natural-number height and an arbitrary function $M$ from natural numbers to natural numbers, and any finite list of inputs, each input having a 32-bit sequence and a natural-number coin height, this function returns an accumulator. If the unsigned version is at least $2$ and flags bit $0$ is set, it starts with integer fields $H=T=-1$ and list $R=[]$ and processes the inputs from left to right: an input with coin height $c$ and sequence bit $31$ set prepends $0$ to $R$ and leaves $H,T$ unchanged; otherwise it prepends $c$ and, writing $d$ for the unsigned value of the lowest sixteen sequence bits, replaces $T$ with $\max(T,M(\max(c-1,0))+512d-1)$ when bit $22$ is set, or replaces $H$ with $\max(H,c+d-1)$ when bit $22$ is unset, leaving the other integer field unchanged. Those updates use integer arithmetic, while the index $\max(c-1,0)$ expresses natural-number subtraction. If the enabling condition is false, the returned integer fields are both $-1$ and the list field is the reverse of the input coin heights in their original order, irrespective of sequence bits. An empty input list returns $(-1,-1,[])$ in either branch. The context height is unused, and there are no restrictions on input heights or on $M$.

**`returnedHeights`.** For any accumulator consisting of two unrestricted integer fields and a finite list of natural numbers named `heightsRev`, this function returns that list in reverse order and ignores the integer fields. The accumulator need not have been produced by any other function, and an empty list returns an empty list.

**`evaluate`.** Given any context consisting of a natural-number height $h$ and an arbitrary function $M$ from natural numbers to natural numbers, and any accumulator with integer fields $H,T$ and a finite natural-number list, this Boolean is true exactly when both strict inequalities $H<h$ and $T<M(\max(h-1,0))$ hold, with the natural-number right sides viewed as integers. The list field is ignored. The index uses natural-number subtraction, so height $0$ compares against $M(0)$; negative integer fields are allowed, and in particular fields $H=T=-1$ satisfy both inequalities for every context. No monotonicity or bound on $M$, or restriction on the accumulator's origin, is assumed.

**`sequenceLocks`.** Given arbitrary 32-bit version and flags, a context with natural-number height $h$ and an arbitrary function $M$ from natural numbers to natural numbers, and any finite list of inputs, each consisting of a 32-bit sequence and natural-number coin height, this Boolean first constructs an accumulator and then tests both strict inequalities $H<h$ and $T<M(\max(h-1,0))$ for its integer fields. When the unsigned version is at least $2$ and flags bit $0$ is set, construction starts with $H=T=-1$ and an empty list and processes inputs from left to right: sequence bit $31$ being set leaves both integer fields unchanged and prepends $0$ to the list; otherwise, for coin height $c$ and lowest-sixteen-bit unsigned value $d$, it prepends $c$ and updates $T$ to $\max(T,M(\max(c-1,0))+512d-1)$ if sequence bit $22$ is set, or updates $H$ to $\max(H,c+d-1)$ if bit $22$ is unset, leaving the other field unchanged. If the enabling condition fails, construction leaves both integer fields equal to $-1$ and uses the reversed list of input coin heights. The constructed list does not affect the Boolean test. Arithmetic in the integer-field updates and comparisons is integer arithmetic, and the indices supplied to $M$ use natural-number subtraction with a floor of $0$. Consequently the result is true for a failed enabling condition or an empty input list, including at context height $0$. No bounds on heights, restrictions on $M$, or conditions comparing input coin heights with the context height are required.

theorem BitcoinBIP68.decode_sequence (sequence : BitVec 32) :
    (BitcoinBIP68.coreDisabled sequence = true ↔ BitcoinBIP68.specDisabled sequence) ∧
    (BitcoinBIP68.coreTimeBased sequence = true ↔ BitcoinBIP68.specTimeBased sequence) ∧
    BitcoinBIP68.coreDelay sequence = BitcoinBIP68.specDelay sequence ∧
    BitcoinBIP68.coreSeconds sequence = 512 * BitcoinBIP68.specDelay sequence := by sorry

Let $s$ be any unsigned 32-bit word and $n$ its value. Put $d=n\bmod65536$. The implementation's disable-bit and time-type tests agree with the corresponding quotient-and-remainder tests, its masked delay is $d$, and its masked left-shifted seconds value is $512d$:

$$\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{disabled}_{\mathrm{core}}(s)&\iff\lfloor n/2^{31}\rfloor=1,\\
\mathrm{time}_{\mathrm{core}}(s)&\iff\lfloor n/2^{22}\rfloor\bmod2=1,\\
\mathrm{delay}_{\mathrm{core}}(s)&=d,\\
\mathrm{seconds}_{\mathrm{core}}(s)&=512d.
\end{aligned}$$

The statement includes every bit pattern and makes no hypothesis on the unused bits. It connects the bit-vector implementation to the arithmetic specification, including the fact that the masked nine-bit shift loses no significant bits.

theorem BitcoinBIP68.fold_acceptance (ctx : BitcoinBIP68.Context)
    (acc : BitcoinBIP68.Accumulator) (inputs : List BitcoinBIP68.Input) :

$$\mathrm{evaluate}(F(A,I))=\mathrm{true}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad

    (hctx : BitcoinBIP68.admissible ctx inputs)

    (BitcoinBIP68.sequenceLocks version flags ctx inputs = true ↔
      BitcoinBIP68.satisfiesBIP68 version flags ctx inputs) ∧
    BitcoinBIP68.returnedHeights (BitcoinBIP68.calculate version flags ctx inputs) =
      BitcoinBIP68.expectedHeights version flags inputs := by sorry

Let $v,f$ be unsigned 32-bit transaction-version and flag words, $H$ the candidate height, $M$ the supplied ancestor median-time function, and $I=[(s_i,c_i)]$ a finite input list. Assume $0<H\le2^{31}-1$, $c_i\le H$, and $0\le M(h)\le2^{63}-1$ for $h\le H$. For each non-disabled input when enforcement is active, also assume the pre-subtraction sum selected by bit 22 fits its signed destination: $c_i+d_i\le2^{31}-1$ when bit 22 is clear (height lock), and $M(\max(c_i-1,0))+512d_i\le2^{63}-1$ when bit 22 is set (time lock), with $d_i=s_i\bmod65536$. Each input is held to the bound of its own lock type, not to either bound.

Let $E$ mean $v\ge2$ and $f\bmod2=1$. Let $P(i)$ mean that bit 31 is set, or that the delay selected by bit 22 has elapsed: $c_i+d_i\le H$ for a height lock and $M(\max(c_i-1,0))+512d_i\le M(H-1)$ for a time lock. This component theorem has two conclusions:

$$\mathrm{SequenceLocks}_{\mathrm{Lean}}(v,f,H,M,I)=\mathrm{true}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \neg E\ \lor\ \forall i\in I,\ P(i),$$

and the returned height list is the original ordered list with $c_i$ replaced by zero exactly when $E$ holds and input $i$ has bit 31 set. No clock monotonicity, nonempty-list assumption, or prior acceptance assumption is imposed.

This is the correctness contract for a Lean transcription of the pinned Core helpers, relative to separately defined arithmetic eligibility and height-list specifications. Coinbase exclusion, supplying the ancestor clocks and spent-output heights, activation selection, and the manual C++-to-Lean correspondence are explicit external boundaries. It does not claim verification of a compiled Bitcoin Core binary.

Within the whole-mainnet mission this is a supporting component. Its caller assumptions must be discharged by the wider validation development; proving this theorem alone does not complete that mission.

## Read-back of `BitcoinBIP68.core_correct`

### Notation used throughout

- A *32-bit word* is a bit-vector of width 32. For such a word $b$, write $\mathrm{val}(b) \in \{0, 1, \dots, 2^{32}-1\}$ for the natural number it encodes, and $b[k]$ for its $k$-th bit ($k = 0$ is the least significant bit). "$b \mathbin{\&} c$" is bitwise AND of two 32-bit words, and "$\ne 0$" on words means "is not the all-zero word".
- All quotients $\lfloor a / m \rfloor$ and remainders $a \bmod m$ are on natural numbers (floor division). Subtraction on natural numbers is *truncated*: $a - 1$ equals $0$ when $a = 0$; where this matters I write $\max(a-1,0)$ explicitly. Subtraction written inside $\mathbb{Z}$ is ordinary integer subtraction.
- $N_{32} := 2147483647 = 2^{31}-1$ and $N_{64} := 9223372036854775807 = 2^{63}-1$ (these are the constants named `int32Max` and `int64Max`).
- $n \ge 0$ is arbitrary; the list of inputs may be empty.

### The objects quantified over

The theorem is universally quantified over:

- two 32-bit words $\mathit{version}$ and $\mathit{flags}$; write $v := \mathrm{val}(\mathit{version})$ and $f := \mathrm{val}(\mathit{flags})$;
- a *context* $C$, consisting of a natural number $H$ (the field `height`) and a **total** function $M : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ (the field `mtp`), defined on every natural number with no constraint beyond those in the hypotheses below;
- a finite list of *inputs* $x_1, \dots, x_n$ ($n \ge 0$), where each input $x_i$ consists of a 32-bit word $s_i$ (the field `sequence`) and a natural number $h_i$ (the field `coinHeight`); write $\sigma_i := \mathrm{val}(s_i)$.

### Auxiliary notions, unfolded

**"Spec-side" predicates (propositions, defined arithmetically on $\mathrm{val}$):**

- $\mathrm{specEnabled}(\mathit{version}, \mathit{flags})$ :$\iff$ $2 \le v \;\wedge\; f \bmod 2 = 1$. (The second conjunct says the least significant bit of $\mathit{flags}$ is $1$.)
- $\mathrm{specDisabled}(s)$ :$\iff$ $\lfloor \mathrm{val}(s) / 2147483648 \rfloor = 1$, i.e. $\lfloor \mathrm{val}(s)/2^{31}\rfloor = 1$. Since $\mathrm{val}(s) < 2^{32}$, this quotient is $0$ or $1$, so this holds exactly when $\mathrm{val}(s) \ge 2^{31}$, i.e. bit 31 of $s$ is set.
- $\mathrm{specTimeBased}(s)$ :$\iff$ $\lfloor \mathrm{val}(s)/4194304 \rfloor \bmod 2 = 1$, i.e. $\lfloor \mathrm{val}(s)/2^{22}\rfloor$ is odd, i.e. bit 22 of $s$ is set.
- $\mathrm{specDelay}(s) := \mathrm{val}(s) \bmod 65536 = \mathrm{val}(s) \bmod 2^{16}$, a natural number in $[0, 65535]$ (the low 16 bits of $s$ read as a number).

- $\mathrm{inputSatisfied}(C, x_i)$ :$\iff$
$$
\mathrm{specDisabled}(s_i) \;\vee\;
\begin{cases}
M\big(\max(h_i - 1, 0)\big) + 512 \cdot \mathrm{specDelay}(s_i) \;\le\; M\big(\max(H-1,0)\big) & \text{if } \mathrm{specTimeBased}(s_i),\\[4pt]
h_i + \mathrm{specDelay}(s_i) \;\le\; H & \text{otherwise.}
\end{cases}
$$
Here the arithmetic is on natural numbers; the arguments $h_i - 1$ and $H - 1$ passed to $M$ are truncated natural subtractions (so if $h_i = 0$, the argument is $M(0)$). The disjunction is inclusive: if $\mathrm{specDisabled}(s_i)$ holds, the input is satisfied regardless of the case analysis.

- $\mathrm{satisfiesBIP68}(\mathit{version}, \mathit{flags}, C, [x_1,\dots,x_n])$ :$\iff$
$$
\neg\,\mathrm{specEnabled}(\mathit{version}, \mathit{flags}) \;\vee\; \forall i \in \{1,\dots,n\},\ \mathrm{inputSatisfied}(C, x_i).
$$
If $n = 0$ the universal clause is vacuously true, so this proposition holds for the empty input list whatever $\mathit{version}$, $\mathit{flags}$, $C$ are.

- $\mathrm{expectedHeights}(\mathit{version}, \mathit{flags}, [x_1,\dots,x_n])$ is the list of natural numbers $[e_1, \dots, e_n]$ (same length $n$, same order) with
$$
e_i := \begin{cases} 0 & \text{if } \mathrm{specEnabled}(\mathit{version},\mathit{flags}) \wedge \mathrm{specDisabled}(s_i),\\ h_i & \text{otherwise.}\end{cases}
$$

**"Core-side" functions (Boolean-valued, defined by bitwise operations):**

- $\mathrm{coreEnabled}(\mathit{version}, \mathit{flags})$ is the Boolean that is `true` exactly when $2 \le v$ **and** the word $\mathit{flags} \mathbin{\&} 1$ is nonzero (i.e. bit 0 of $\mathit{flags}$ is set).
- $\mathrm{coreDisabled}(s)$ is `true` exactly when $s \mathbin{\&} \mathtt{0x80000000} \ne 0$ (bit 31 of $s$ is set).
- $\mathrm{coreTimeBased}(s)$ is `true` exactly when $s \mathbin{\&} \mathtt{0x00400000} \ne 0$ (bit 22 of $s$ is set).
- $\mathrm{coreDelay}(s) := \mathrm{val}(s \mathbin{\&} \mathtt{0x0000ffff})$, the low 16 bits of $s$ as a natural number in $[0, 65535]$.
- $\mathrm{coreSeconds}(s) := \mathrm{val}\big((s \mathbin{\&} \mathtt{0x0000ffff}) \ll 9\big)$, where $\ll 9$ is a left shift by 9 positions inside a 32-bit word. Because the masked word is below $2^{16}$, shifting it left by $9$ stays below $2^{25} < 2^{32}$, so no bits are lost and $\mathrm{coreSeconds}(s) = 512 \cdot \mathrm{coreDelay}(s)$.

- An *accumulator* is a triple $A = (m_H, m_T, L)$ with $m_H \in \mathbb{Z}$ (`minHeight`), $m_T \in \mathbb{Z}$ (`minTime`), and $L$ a list of natural numbers (`heightsRev`). The initial accumulator is $A_0 := (-1, -1, [\,])$.

- One step $\mathrm{coreStep}(C, A, x_i)$, for $A = (m_H, m_T, L)$, yields:
  - if $\mathrm{coreDisabled}(s_i)$: $(m_H,\ m_T,\ 0 :: L)$ — the minima are untouched and $0$ is prepended to $L$;
  - else if $\mathrm{coreTimeBased}(s_i)$: $\big(m_H,\ \max\big(m_T,\ M(\max(h_i-1,0)) + \mathrm{coreSeconds}(s_i) - 1\big),\ h_i :: L\big)$, where the sum and the "$-1$" are computed in $\mathbb{Z}$ after casting the two natural numbers to integers (so the result can be $-1$ when both summands are $0$), while the argument $h_i - 1$ of $M$ is a truncated natural subtraction;
  - else: $\big(\max\big(m_H,\ h_i + \mathrm{coreDelay}(s_i) - 1\big),\ m_T,\ h_i :: L\big)$, again with the sum and "$-1$" in $\mathbb{Z}$.

- $\mathrm{calculate}(\mathit{version}, \mathit{flags}, C, [x_1,\dots,x_n])$ is the accumulator
  - $A_n$, where $A_k := \mathrm{coreStep}(C, A_{k-1}, x_k)$ for $k = 1,\dots,n$ (a left fold, processing inputs in list order starting from $A_0$), **if** $\mathrm{coreEnabled}(\mathit{version}, \mathit{flags})$ is `true`;
  - $\big(-1,\ -1,\ \mathrm{reverse}([h_1,\dots,h_n])\big)$ **otherwise**.

  Unwinding the fold in the enabled case: $A_n = (m_H^\ast, m_T^\ast, L^\ast)$ where
  $$
  m_H^\ast = \max\Big(\{-1\} \cup \{\, h_i + \mathrm{coreDelay}(s_i) - 1 : \neg\mathrm{coreDisabled}(s_i),\ \neg\mathrm{coreTimeBased}(s_i) \,\}\Big),
  $$
  $$
  m_T^\ast = \max\Big(\{-1\} \cup \{\, M(\max(h_i-1,0)) + \mathrm{coreSeconds}(s_i) - 1 : \neg\mathrm{coreDisabled}(s_i),\ \mathrm{coreTimeBased}(s_i) \,\}\Big),
  $$
  (maxima in $\mathbb{Z}$) and $L^\ast$ is the list $[g_n, g_{n-1}, \dots, g_1]$ with $g_i := 0$ if $\mathrm{coreDisabled}(s_i)$ and $g_i := h_i$ otherwise.

- $\mathrm{returnedHeights}(A) := \mathrm{reverse}(L)$ for $A = (m_H, m_T, L)$.

- $\mathrm{evaluate}(C, A)$ is the Boolean that is `true` exactly when, in $\mathbb{Z}$,
$$
m_H < H \quad\wedge\quad m_T < M\big(\max(H-1,0)\big),
$$
with $H$ and $M(\cdot)$ cast from $\mathbb{N}$ to $\mathbb{Z}$.

- $\mathrm{sequenceLocks}(\mathit{version}, \mathit{flags}, C, \mathit{inputs}) := \mathrm{evaluate}\big(C,\ \mathrm{calculate}(\mathit{version}, \mathit{flags}, C, \mathit{inputs})\big)$, a Boolean.

### The two hypotheses

**Hypothesis $\mathrm{hctx}$ — $\mathrm{admissible}(C, [x_1,\dots,x_n])$:** all four of
1. $0 < H$;
2. $H \le N_{32} = 2^{31}-1$;
3. for every natural number $h$ with $h \le H$: $M(h) \le N_{64} = 2^{63}-1$ (nothing is assumed about $M(h)$ for $h > H$);
4. for every $i \in \{1,\dots,n\}$: $h_i \le H$.

Because of (1), $H - 1$ is an honest subtraction ($H - 1 \ge 0$ and $(H-1)+1 = H$). Nothing forces $h_i > 0$, so $h_i - 1$ may still truncate to $0$.

**Hypothesis $\mathrm{hsafe}$ — $\mathrm{noOverflow}(\mathit{version}, \mathit{flags}, C, [x_1,\dots,x_n])$:** for every $i \in \{1,\dots,n\}$, if $\mathrm{specEnabled}(\mathit{version},\mathit{flags})$ holds and $\mathrm{specDisabled}(s_i)$ does **not** hold, then
$$
\begin{cases}
M\big(\max(h_i-1,0)\big) + 512 \cdot \mathrm{specDelay}(s_i) \;\le\; N_{64} & \text{if } \mathrm{specTimeBased}(s_i),\\[4pt]
h_i + \mathrm{specDelay}(s_i) \;\le\; N_{32} & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases}
$$
(natural-number arithmetic). This hypothesis is vacuous for inputs whose sequence word has bit 31 set, is vacuous when $\mathrm{specEnabled}$ fails, and is vacuous when $n = 0$. Both hypotheses are expressed with the *spec-side* (arithmetic) predicates, not the core-side (bitwise) ones.

Both hypotheses are satisfiable (e.g. $H = 1$, $M \equiv 0$, no inputs), so the theorem is not vacuous as a whole; but it asserts nothing about any $(\mathit{version}, \mathit{flags}, C, \mathit{inputs})$ that violates either hypothesis.

### The conclusion

Under the hypotheses above, the theorem asserts the conjunction of two statements.

**(A) Lock-evaluation agreement (an "if and only if"):**
$$
\mathrm{sequenceLocks}(\mathit{version}, \mathit{flags}, C, [x_1,\dots,x_n]) = \mathtt{true}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\mathrm{satisfiesBIP68}(\mathit{version}, \mathit{flags}, C, [x_1,\dots,x_n]).
$$
The left-hand side is the proposition that a Boolean equals `true`; fully unfolded it says: letting $A = (m_H, m_T, L)$ be $\mathrm{calculate}(\ldots)$ as described above (the fold $A_n$ if $\mathrm{coreEnabled}$ is `true`, else $(-1,-1,\mathrm{reverse}[h_1,\dots,h_n])$), one has $m_H < H$ and $m_T < M(H-1)$ in $\mathbb{Z}$. The right-hand side is the proposition: either $\neg(2 \le v \wedge f \bmod 2 = 1)$, or every input $x_i$ satisfies $\mathrm{inputSatisfied}(C, x_i)$ as unfolded above.

Edge cases contained in (A):
- If $\mathrm{coreEnabled}$ is `false`, the left side reads $-1 < H \wedge -1 < M(H-1)$, which holds because $H$ and $M(H-1)$ are casts of natural numbers.
- If $n = 0$, the left side reads $-1 < H \wedge -1 < M(H-1)$ (the fold returns $A_0$), and the right side holds vacuously.
- On the core side, comparisons are strict ($<$) against thresholds of the form "$\ldots - 1$" in $\mathbb{Z}$; on the spec side, comparisons are non-strict ($\le$) in $\mathbb{N}$ without the "$-1$".
- On the core side an input with $\mathrm{coreDisabled}(s_i)$ contributes nothing to $m_H, m_T$; on the spec side an input with $\mathrm{specDisabled}(s_i)$ is satisfied outright.

**(B) Returned-heights agreement (an equality of lists of natural numbers):**
$$
\mathrm{returnedHeights}\big(\mathrm{calculate}(\mathit{version}, \mathit{flags}, C, [x_1,\dots,x_n])\big)
\;=\;
\mathrm{expectedHeights}(\mathit{version}, \mathit{flags}, [x_1,\dots,x_n]).
$$
Unfolded, the left-hand list is:
- $[g_1, \dots, g_n]$ with $g_i = 0$ if bit 31 of $s_i$ is set and $g_i = h_i$ otherwise, **if** $\mathrm{coreEnabled}(\mathit{version},\mathit{flags})$ is `true` (i.e. $2 \le v$ and bit 0 of $\mathit{flags}$ is set);
- $[h_1, \dots, h_n]$ (the reverse of the reversed coin-height list) **otherwise**.

The right-hand list is $[e_1,\dots,e_n]$ with $e_i = 0$ if ($2 \le v \wedge f \bmod 2 = 1$) and $\lfloor \sigma_i / 2^{31}\rfloor = 1$, and $e_i = h_i$ otherwise. Both lists have length $n$ and preserve input order; for $n = 0$ both are the empty list. Note that $\mathrm{expectedHeights}$ does not depend on the context $C$, whereas the left-hand side is computed from $\mathrm{calculate}$, which takes $C$ as an argument (though $C$ only enters the $m_H, m_T$ components, not $L$).

### Summary in one sentence

For all 32-bit words $\mathit{version}, \mathit{flags}$, every context $C = (H, M)$ with $M$ a total function $\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, and every finite (possibly empty) list of inputs $(s_i, h_i)_{i=1}^n$, **if** $0 < H \le 2^{31}-1$, $M(h) \le 2^{63}-1$ for all $h \le H$, every $h_i \le H$, **and** for every input with $2 \le v$, $f$ odd, and bit 31 of $s_i$ clear the quantity $M(\max(h_i-1,0)) + 512(\sigma_i \bmod 2^{16})$ (if bit 22 of $s_i$ is set) resp. $h_i + (\sigma_i \bmod 2^{16})$ (otherwise) is at most $2^{63}-1$ resp. $2^{31}-1$, **then** (A) the Boolean $\mathrm{sequenceLocks}$ computed by the bitwise/integer-accumulator fold is `true` exactly when the arithmetic proposition $\mathrm{satisfiesBIP68}$ holds, **and** (B) the list of heights read off that fold's accumulator equals, entry by entry, the list $\mathrm{expectedHeights}$ defined arithmetically.

items.theorem_title: Block subsidy, issuance schedule, and cumulative issuance
items.natural_language_statement:
Amounts are counted in satoshi. One bitcoin is $\mathrm{COIN} = 10^{8}$ satoshi and $\mathrm{MAX\_MONEY} = 21{,}000{,}000 \cdot \mathrm{COIN} = 2.1 \times 10^{15}$ satoshi. The mainnet halving interval is $I = 210{,}000$ blocks.

The **Core subsidy** at a block height $h \in \mathbb N$ transcribes `GetBlockSubsidy` at mainnet parameters. With $k = \lfloor h / I \rfloor$ halvings, the subsidy is $0$ when $k \ge 64$, and otherwise the right shift $(50 \cdot \mathrm{COIN}) \gg k$. Heights are nonnegative in the source and the shifted value is nonnegative, so natural numbers represent both exactly; the explicit $k \ge 64$ branch mirrors the source's guard against an undefined shift.

The **declarative schedule** is
$$\mathrm{specSubsidy}(h) = \left\lfloor \frac{50 \cdot \mathrm{COIN}}{2^{\lfloor h / I \rfloor}} \right\rfloor ,$$
fifty bitcoin halved once per interval with the remainder discarded.

**Cumulative issuance** below height $n$ is the running sum $\mathrm{issuedBelow}(0) = 0$, $\mathrm{issuedBelow}(n+1) = \mathrm{issuedBelow}(n) + \mathrm{coreSubsidy}(n)$. The **interval sum** $\mathrm{intervalSum}(m) = \sum_{j<m} \lfloor 50 \cdot \mathrm{COIN} / 2^{j} \rfloor$ collects one subsidy per interval. The **zero height** is $33 I = 6{,}930{,}000$, the first height whose subsidy the theorems show to be zero.

These definitions are the inputs for the issuance theorems and for any later ledger-supply argument, which will cite the cumulative issuance as its upper bound.

**Formalization Note.** All quantities are natural numbers. The shift is Lean's `>>>` on `Nat`, which is exact division by a power of two; the recursive definitions are structural so that proofs proceed by induction on height or interval count. Only `Std` is imported.
items.definition:
import Std

namespace BitcoinSubsidy

/-- `consensus/amount.h`: `COIN{100'000'000}`, the number of satoshis in one bitcoin. -/
def COIN : Nat := 100000000

/-- `consensus/amount.h`: `MAX_MONEY{21'000'000 * COIN}`, the consensus sanity bound on amounts. -/
def MAX_MONEY : Nat := 21000000 * COIN

/-- `kernel/chainparams.cpp`, `CMainParams`: `consensus.nSubsidyHalvingInterval = 210000`. -/
def halvingInterval : Nat := 210000

/-- Transcription of `GetBlockSubsidy` (`validation.cpp`) at mainnet parameters.
Block heights are nonnegative, and the `CAmount` right shift `nSubsidy >>= halvings` acts on the
nonnegative value `50 * COIN`, so it is division by `2 ^ halvings`; the source returns `0`
outright once `halvings >= 64`, where the C++ shift would be undefined. -/
def coreSubsidy (height : Nat) : Nat :=
  let halvings := height / halvingInterval
  if 64 ≤ halvings then 0 else (50 * COIN) >>> halvings

/-- Declarative issuance schedule: fifty bitcoin, halved once per `halvingInterval` blocks. -/
def specSubsidy (height : Nat) : Nat := (50 * COIN) / 2 ^ (height / halvingInterval)

/-- Total subsidy of all blocks at heights `0, 1, …, n - 1`, as `GetBlockSubsidy` computes it. -/
def issuedBelow : Nat → Nat
  | 0 => 0
  | n + 1 => issuedBelow n + coreSubsidy n

/-- Sum of the per-interval subsidies for the first `m` intervals. -/
def intervalSum : Nat → Nat
  | 0 => 0
  | m + 1 => intervalSum m + (50 * COIN) / 2 ^ m

/-- The first height whose subsidy is zero: thirty-three halvings. -/
def zeroHeight : Nat := 33 * halvingInterval

end BitcoinSubsidy

## Read-back: definition file `Def_BitcoinSubsidy`

All objects below live in the natural numbers $\mathbb{N} = \{0, 1, 2, \dots\}$. Throughout, "$/$" on natural numbers is **truncating (floor) division**: $a / b = \lfloor a / b \rfloor$, and $a / 0 = 0$. There are no negative numbers anywhere in this file.

---

**`COIN`.** A fixed natural number constant:
$$\mathrm{COIN} = 100{,}000{,}000 = 10^{8}.$$
It carries no other structure; it is simply the number one hundred million.

---

**`MAX_MONEY`.** A fixed natural number constant defined as the product
$$\mathrm{MAX\_MONEY} = 21{,}000{,}000 \cdot \mathrm{COIN} = 21{,}000{,}000 \cdot 10^{8} = 2{,}100{,}000{,}000{,}000{,}000 = 2.1 \times 10^{15}.$$

---

**`halvingInterval`.** A fixed natural number constant:
$$\mathrm{halvingInterval} = 210{,}000.$$

---

**`coreSubsidy`.** A function $\mathrm{coreSubsidy} : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$. For a natural number input $h$ (called "height"), first form the truncated quotient
$$k = h / 210{,}000 = \left\lfloor \frac{h}{210{,}000} \right\rfloor .$$
Then the value is defined by a two-way case split on $k$:

- if $64 \le k$, the value is $0$;
- otherwise (i.e. if $k \le 63$), the value is the natural number $50 \cdot \mathrm{COIN} = 5{,}000{,}000{,}000$ shifted right by $k$ binary digits. On natural numbers a right shift by $k$ bits equals truncating division by $2^k$, so this branch equals
$$\left\lfloor \frac{5{,}000{,}000{,}000}{2^{k}} \right\rfloor .$$

So, written in one formula with $k = \lfloor h / 210{,}000 \rfloor$:
$$\mathrm{coreSubsidy}(h) = \begin{cases} 0 & \text{if } k \ge 64,\\[4pt] \left\lfloor 5{,}000{,}000{,}000 / 2^{k} \right\rfloor & \text{if } k \le 63. \end{cases}$$

Edge cases that the definition literally includes: at $h = 0$ one has $k = 0$ and the value is $5{,}000{,}000{,}000 / 2^0 = 5{,}000{,}000{,}000$. For every $h$ with $0 \le h \le 209{,}999$ the quotient $k$ is $0$ and the value is likewise $5{,}000{,}000{,}000$; the quotient $k$ increases by exactly $1$ each time $h$ crosses a multiple of $210{,}000$. Because the shift is truncating, for values of $k$ at which $2^k$ exceeds $5{,}000{,}000{,}000$ the second branch already yields $0$ by truncation, independently of the $k \ge 64$ branch. The first branch (value $0$ when $k \ge 64$, i.e. when $h \ge 64 \cdot 210{,}000 = 13{,}440{,}000$) is an explicit case in the definition, not a consequence of the arithmetic. The function is total: every natural number input produces a natural number output.

---

**`specSubsidy`.** A function $\mathrm{specSubsidy} : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ given by a single formula with **no** case split:
$$\mathrm{specSubsidy}(h) = \left\lfloor \frac{50 \cdot \mathrm{COIN}}{2^{\lfloor h / 210{,}000 \rfloor}} \right\rfloor = \left\lfloor \frac{5{,}000{,}000{,}000}{2^{\lfloor h / 210{,}000 \rfloor}} \right\rfloor .$$
Here the exponent $\lfloor h / 210{,}000 \rfloor$ is a natural number, $2^{(\cdot)}$ is natural-number exponentiation (so the divisor $2^{\lfloor h/210{,}000\rfloor}$ is always at least $1$ and never zero), and the outer division truncates. Unlike `coreSubsidy`, there is no special branch at $64$ halvings; for arbitrarily large $h$ the formula is still evaluated as written, and once $2^{\lfloor h/210{,}000\rfloor} > 5{,}000{,}000{,}000$ the truncating division returns $0$. At $h = 0$ the value is $5{,}000{,}000{,}000$.

---

**`issuedBelow`.** A function $\mathrm{issuedBelow} : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ defined by recursion on its argument:

- base case: $\mathrm{issuedBelow}(0) = 0$;
- step: $\mathrm{issuedBelow}(n+1) = \mathrm{issuedBelow}(n) + \mathrm{coreSubsidy}(n)$.

Unfolding the recursion, for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$,
$$\mathrm{issuedBelow}(n) = \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} \mathrm{coreSubsidy}(i),$$
the sum of $\mathrm{coreSubsidy}$ over the heights $0, 1, \dots, n-1$ (the empty sum, equal to $0$, when $n = 0$). Note that the summand added at the step from $n$ to $n+1$ is $\mathrm{coreSubsidy}(n)$, the subsidy at height $n$ itself, so $\mathrm{issuedBelow}(n)$ **excludes** height $n$ and includes height $0$. items.formal_statement: theorem BitcoinSubsidy.core_eq_spec (height : Nat) : coreSubsidy height = specSubsidy height := by sorry
items.natural_language_statement:
For every block height $h \in \mathbb N$, the transcription of `GetBlockSubsidy` and the declarative halving schedule agree:
$$\mathrm{coreSubsidy}(h) = \left\lfloor \frac{50 \cdot \mathrm{COIN}}{2^{\lfloor h / 210000 \rfloor}} \right\rfloor .$$

**Binders.** One universally quantified variable: a natural number $h \in \mathbb{N} = \{0, 1, 2, \dots\}$ (named "height"). There are no hypotheses; the claim is asserted for every natural number $h$ without exception, including $h = 0$ and arbitrarily large $h$.

**Statement.** For every $h \in \mathbb{N}$,
$$\mathrm{coreSubsidy}(h) = \mathrm{specSubsidy}(h),$$
an equality of natural numbers, where the two sides unfold as follows. Write $k = \lfloor h / 210{,}000 \rfloor$ (truncating natural-number division by the constant $\mathrm{halvingInterval} = 210{,}000$). The left-hand side is
$$\mathrm{coreSubsidy}(h) = \begin{cases} 0 & \text{if } 64 \le k,\\[4pt] \left\lfloor 5{,}000{,}000{,}000 / 2^{k} \right\rfloor & \text{if } k \le 63, \end{cases}$$
where $5{,}000{,}000{,}000 = 50 \cdot \mathrm{COIN}$ with $\mathrm{COIN} = 10^8$, and the second branch is literally a right shift of the natural number $5{,}000{,}000{,}000$ by $k$ bits (which on natural numbers equals truncating division by $2^k$). The right-hand side is the single-formula value with no case split,
$$\mathrm{specSubsidy}(h) = \left\lfloor \frac{5{,}000{,}000{,}000}{2^{k}} \right\rfloor ,$$
again with truncating natural-number division and natural-number exponentiation $2^k \ge 1$.

**What is literally asserted.** For every $h$, the case-split definition and the case-free formula produce the same natural number. In particular, this asserts that for every $h$ with $k = \lfloor h / 210{,}000 \rfloor \ge 64$ (i.e. $h \ge 13{,}440{,}000$), the value $\lfloor 5{,}000{,}000{,}000 / 2^{k} \rfloor$ equals $0$, and that for every $h$ with $k \le 63$ the right shift by $k$ equals the truncated quotient by $2^k$. At $h = 0$ both sides are $5{,}000{,}000{,}000$ by their definitions.

## Read-back: theorem `BitcoinSubsidy.subsidy_antitone`

**Binders.** Two universally quantified natural numbers $h_1, h_2 \in \mathbb{N} = \{0, 1, 2, \dots\}$, and one hypothesis
$$h_1 \le h_2$$
(non-strict; the case $h_1 = h_2$ is included, as are $h_1 = 0$ and arbitrarily large $h_2$). The hypothesis is satisfiable for every $h_1$ (e.g. by $h_2 = h_1$), so the statement is never vacuous.

**Statement.** For all $h_1, h_2 \in \mathbb{N}$ with $h_1 \le h_2$,
$$\mathrm{coreSubsidy}(h_2) \le \mathrm{coreSubsidy}(h_1),$$
a non-strict inequality of natural numbers: the value at the larger-or-equal height is at most the value at the smaller-or-equal height. Here, for any height $h$, writing $k = \lfloor h / 210{,}000 \rfloor$ (truncating division by $\mathrm{halvingInterval} = 210{,}000$),
$$\mathrm{coreSubsidy}(h) = \begin{cases} 0 & \text{if } 64 \le k,\\[4pt] \left\lfloor 5{,}000{,}000{,}000 / 2^{k} \right\rfloor & \text{if } k \le 63, \end{cases}$$
where $5{,}000{,}000{,}000 = 50 \cdot \mathrm{COIN}$ with $\mathrm{COIN} = 10^{8}$, and the second branch is a right shift of $5{,}000{,}000{,}000$ by $k$ bits (equivalently, truncating division by $2^k$).

**What is literally asserted.** The function $\mathrm{coreSubsidy} : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is non-increasing (weakly antitone) with respect to the usual order on $\mathbb{N}$: increasing the height never increases the value. It does **not** assert strict decrease anywhere; in particular, two heights in the same block of $210{,}000$ (same quotient $k$) have equal values and the statement is consistent with that, and two heights both at or beyond $64 \cdot 210{,}000 = 13{,}440{,}000$ both give $0$. The statement covers all pairs, including pairs straddling the switch from the second branch to the $k \ge 64$ branch. Nothing is said about `specSubsidy`.

## Read-back: theorem `BitcoinSubsidy.subsidy_halving`

**Binders.** One universally quantified natural number $h \in \mathbb{N} = \{0, 1, 2, \dots\}$ (named "height"). No hypotheses; the claim is made for every $h$, including $h = 0$ and arbitrarily large $h$.

**Statement.** For every $h \in \mathbb{N}$,
$$\mathrm{coreSubsidy}(h + 210{,}000) = \left\lfloor \frac{\mathrm{coreSubsidy}(h)}{2} \right\rfloor ,$$
where $210{,}000 = \mathrm{halvingInterval}$ and the division by $2$ on the right-hand side is **truncating natural-number division** (so if $\mathrm{coreSubsidy}(h)$ is odd, the right-hand side is $(\mathrm{coreSubsidy}(h) - 1)/2$, and if $\mathrm{coreSubsidy}(h) = 1$ the right-hand side is $0$).

Both sides unfold via the definition: for any height $x$, with $k_x = \lfloor x / 210{,}000 \rfloor$,
$$\mathrm{coreSubsidy}(x) = \begin{cases} 0 & \text{if } 64 \le k_x,\\[4pt] \left\lfloor 5{,}000{,}000{,}000 / 2^{k_x} \right\rfloor & \text{if } k_x \le 63, \end{cases}$$
with $5{,}000{,}000{,}000 = 50 \cdot \mathrm{COIN}$, $\mathrm{COIN} = 10^8$, and the second branch a right shift of $5{,}000{,}000{,}000$ by $k_x$ bits. Note that $\lfloor (h + 210{,}000) / 210{,}000 \rfloor = \lfloor h / 210{,}000 \rfloor + 1$, so the left-hand side uses one more halving than the right-hand side's inner value.

**What is literally asserted.** Moving the height forward by exactly $210{,}000$ changes the value from $\mathrm{coreSubsidy}(h)$ to its truncated half. The statement covers, in particular:

- heights $h$ with $\lfloor h / 210{,}000 \rfloor = 63$, for which the left-hand side falls into the explicit $64 \le k$ branch and equals $0$, so the statement there asserts $0 = \lfloor \mathrm{coreSubsidy}(h) / 2 \rfloor$;
- heights $h$ with $\lfloor h / 210{,}000 \rfloor \ge 64$, for which both sides are $0$ by the first branch;
- the general case $k_h \le 62$, where the statement asserts $\lfloor 5{,}000{,}000{,}000 / 2^{k_h + 1} \rfloor = \lfloor \lfloor 5{,}000{,}000{,}000 / 2^{k_h} \rfloor / 2 \rfloor$, an identity between two truncated divisions.

The statement is an equality (not merely $\le$), it concerns only shifts by exactly one interval of $210{,}000$ (not by a general multiple), and it says nothing about `specSubsidy`.

$$\mathrm{coreSubsidy}(h) = 0 \iff h \ge 33 \cdot 210000 = 6{,}930{,}000 .$$

## Read-back: theorem `BitcoinSubsidy.subsidy_zero_iff`

**Binders.** One universally quantified natural number $h \in \mathbb{N} = \{0, 1, 2, \dots\}$ (named "height"). No hypotheses; the claim is made for every $h$, including $h = 0$ and arbitrarily large $h$.

**Statement.** For every $h \in \mathbb{N}$, the following two propositions are **equivalent** (biconditional, both directions):
$$\mathrm{coreSubsidy}(h) = 0 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \mathrm{zeroHeight} \le h .$$
The right-hand proposition is the **non-strict** inequality with the constant
$$\mathrm{zeroHeight} = 33 \cdot \mathrm{halvingInterval} = 33 \cdot 210{,}000 = 6{,}930{,}000,$$
i.e. it says $6{,}930{,}000 \le h$ (so $h = 6{,}930{,}000$ itself satisfies the right-hand side, while $h = 6{,}929{,}999$ does not). The left-hand proposition says that the natural number
$$\mathrm{coreSubsidy}(h) = \begin{cases} 0 & \text{if } 64 \le k,\\[4pt] \left\lfloor 5{,}000{,}000{,}000 / 2^{k} \right\rfloor & \text{if } k \le 63, \end{cases} \qquad k = \lfloor h / 210{,}000 \rfloor,$$
equals exactly $0$, where $5{,}000{,}000{,}000 = 50 \cdot \mathrm{COIN}$, $\mathrm{COIN} = 10^8$, the quotient $k$ is truncating natural-number division, and the second branch is a right shift of $5{,}000{,}000{,}000$ by $k$ bits (truncating division by $2^k$).

**What is literally asserted.** Two claims at once, for every $h$:

- (forward direction) if $\mathrm{coreSubsidy}(h) = 0$ then $h \ge 6{,}930{,}000$; equivalently, every height $h \le 6{,}929{,}999$ (every $h$ with $\lfloor h / 210{,}000 \rfloor \le 32$) has $\mathrm{coreSubsidy}(h) \ne 0$, i.e. a strictly positive value;
- (backward direction) if $h \ge 6{,}930{,}000$ then $\mathrm{coreSubsidy}(h) = 0$; this covers both the heights with $33 \le \lfloor h / 210{,}000 \rfloor \le 63$, where the value is the truncated quotient $\lfloor 5{,}000{,}000{,}000 / 2^{k} \rfloor$ and the statement asserts this quotient is $0$, and the heights with $\lfloor h / 210{,}000 \rfloor \ge 64$ ($h \ge 13{,}440{,}000$), where the value is $0$ by the explicit first branch.

So the set of heights at which `coreSubsidy` is zero is asserted to be exactly $\{h \in \mathbb{N} : h \ge 6{,}930{,}000\}$. The statement concerns `coreSubsidy` only, not `specSubsidy`, and says nothing about the nonzero values themselves beyond their being nonzero.

$$\mathrm{issuedBelow}(n) \le 2{,}099{,}999{,}997{,}690{,}000 .$$

items.natural_language_statement:
For every $n \in \mathbb N$, the cumulative subsidy of all blocks at heights below $n$ is strictly less than the consensus amount bound:
$$\mathrm{issuedBelow}(n) < \mathrm{MAX\_MONEY} = 21{,}000{,}000 \cdot 10^{8}.$$
Here $\mathrm{issuedBelow}(n) = \sum_{h < n} \mathrm{coreSubsidy}(h)$ with $\mathrm{coreSubsidy}$ the transcription of `GetBlockSubsidy` at mainnet parameters.

This is the arithmetic content of the twenty-one-million cap: no chain length, however long, lets the subsidy schedule issue `MAX_MONEY` or more. It is stated as a strict inequality against the named constant rather than as an exact value, so that it is the weakest statement a ledger-supply argument needs and remains true under any refinement of the exact total.

**Formalization Note.** The bound concerns the subsidy schedule only. Fees, unclaimed coinbase value and unspendable outputs are matters for the UTXO transition and are not modeled here.

items.theorem_title: Compact targets, proof of work, and difficulty retargeting at mainnet parameters
items.natural_language_statement:
This file transcribes the mainnet proof-of-work arithmetic of Bitcoin Core. An `arith_uint256` is modelled by its value, a natural number below $2^{256}$ (`width`); its left shift and its multiplications discard carries out of the top word, so they reduce modulo $2^{256}$, and its division is exact integer division.

**Parameters.** $\mathrm{powLimit} = 2^{224} - 1$, the target timespan $T = 14 \cdot 24 \cdot 60 \cdot 60 = 1{,}209{,}600$ seconds, the target spacing $600$ seconds, and the difficulty adjustment interval $T / 600 = 2016$ blocks.

**Compact words.** For a 32-bit word $c$: the size $S = \lfloor c / 2^{24} \rfloor$ and the mantissa $W = c \mathbin{\&} \mathtt{0x007fffff}$. `SetCompact` yields $\lfloor W / 2^{8(3-S)} \rfloor$ when $S \le 3$ and $(W \cdot 2^{8(S-3)}) \bmod 2^{256}$ otherwise. The word is **negative** when $W \ne 0$ and $c \mathbin{\&} \mathtt{0x00800000} \ne 0$; it **overflows** when $W \ne 0$ and ($S > 34$, or $W > \mathtt{0xff}$ and $S > 33$, or $W > \mathtt{0xffff}$ and $S > 32$). The **exact value** $\mathrm{specTarget}(c)$ is the same formula without the reduction modulo $2^{256}$.

**Encoding.** `bitLength` is $0$ at $0$ and $\lfloor \log_2 v \rfloor + 1$ otherwise. `GetCompact` of $v$ sets $S = \lfloor (\mathrm{bitLength}(v) + 7) / 8 \rfloor$, forms the mantissa as $((v \bmod 2^{64}) \cdot 2^{8(3-S)}) \bmod 2^{32}$ when $S \le 3$ and as $((\lfloor v / 2^{8(S-3)} \rfloor \bmod 2^{64}) \bmod 2^{32})$ otherwise; if bit 23 of the mantissa is set it divides the mantissa by $256$ and increments $S$; the result is the 32-bit word mantissa $\lor (S \cdot 2^{24})$.

**Validation.** `deriveTarget` returns the decoded value unless the word is negative, decodes to $0$, overflows, or exceeds $\mathrm{powLimit}$. `checkProofOfWork`(hash, word) holds when a target is derived and $\mathrm{hash} \le$ target. `clampTimespan` raises a signed timespan to $T/4$ and lowers it to $4T$. `calculateNextWork`(last word, last time, first time) decodes the last word, multiplies by the clamped elapsed time modulo $2^{256}$, divides by $T$, caps at $\mathrm{powLimit}$, and re-encodes. `permittedTransition`(height, old, new) at a height divisible by $2016$ requires the decoded new word to lie between the re-encoded caps of old $\cdot (T/4) / T$ and old $\cdot 4T / T$ (products modulo $2^{256}$); at other heights it requires old $=$ new. `nextWorkRequired` returns the last word unless the next height is divisible by $2016$, in which case it retargets.

These definitions fix the meaning of `nBits` on the wire and the retarget rule, as inputs for header validation.

**Formalization Note.** Compact words are `BitVec 32` read through `toNat`; values are `Nat`; block times are `Int`, converted with `Int.toNat` only after clamping. `fPowAllowMinDifficultyBlocks`, `fPowNoRetargeting`, and `enforce_BIP94` are fixed to `false` as on mainnet. Only `Std` is imported.
