# Read-back: `Def_BitcoinUtxo.lean` (namespace `BitcoinUtxo`)

Throughout the file there is a standing assumption: $T$ is an arbitrary type (the type of transaction identifiers) equipped with a decidable equality, i.e. for any $a, b \in T$ it can be decided whether $a = b$. Every declaration below that mentions $T$ carries these two implicit assumptions. Nothing else is assumed about $T$: it may be empty, finite, or infinite, and no hash function or structure is attached to it.

---

**`COIN`.** An integer constant: $\mathrm{COIN} = 100{,}000{,}000 = 10^8$ (an element of $\mathbb{Z}$).

---

**`MAX_MONEY`.** An integer constant: $\mathrm{MAX\_MONEY} = 21{,}000{,}000 \cdot \mathrm{COIN} = 2{,}100{,}000{,}000{,}000{,}000 = 2.1 \times 10^{15}$ (an element of $\mathbb{Z}$).

---

**`moneyRange`.** A Boolean-valued function on integers: for $v \in \mathbb{Z}$,
$$\mathrm{moneyRange}(v) = \mathrm{true} \iff 0 \le v \ \text{and}\ v \le \mathrm{MAX\_MONEY},$$
and $\mathrm{moneyRange}(v) = \mathrm{false}$ otherwise. Both inequalities are non-strict; $v = 0$ and $v = \mathrm{MAX\_MONEY}$ pass.

---

**`COINBASE_MATURITY`.** A natural-number constant: $\mathrm{COINBASE\_MATURITY} = 100$ (an element of $\mathbb{N}$).

---

**`OutPoint`** (parametrised by a type $T$). A record with two fields: $\mathrm{txid} \in T$ and $\mathrm{n} \in \mathbb{N}$. Two outpoints are equal exactly when both fields agree; equality of outpoints is decidable (this is derived, and requires decidable equality on $T$). I write an outpoint as $\langle t, i\rangle$.

---

**`TxOut`.** A record with two fields: $\mathrm{value} \in \mathbb{Z}$ (any integer, possibly negative or larger than $\mathrm{MAX\_MONEY}$) and $\mathrm{unspendable} \in \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$. Equality is decidable and componentwise.

---

**`Coin`.** A record with three fields: $\mathrm{out} \in \mathrm{TxOut}$, $\mathrm{height} \in \mathbb{N}$, and $\mathrm{isCoinbase} \in \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$. Equality is decidable and componentwise. For a coin $c$ I write $c.\mathrm{out}.\mathrm{value}$ for the integer value of its output and $c.\mathrm{out}.\mathrm{unspendable}$ for its unspendable flag.

---

**`Tx`** (parametrised by a type $T$). A record with four fields: $\mathrm{txid} \in T$; $\mathrm{vin}$, a finite list of outpoints over $T$ (possibly empty, possibly with repetitions); $\mathrm{vout}$, a finite list of `TxOut` records (possibly empty); and $\mathrm{isCoinbase} \in \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$. Note that $\mathrm{isCoinbase}$ is an independent Boolean field: it is *not* computed from $\mathrm{vin}$, and nothing in the record ties it to the contents of $\mathrm{vin}$. No decidable equality is derived for `Tx`.

---

**`UtxoSet`** (parametrised by a type $T$). A synonym for "finite list of pairs $(p, c)$ with $p$ an outpoint over $T$ and $c$ a coin". The list is ordered and may contain repeated outpoints; distinctness of outpoints is *not* part of this type, it is a separate predicate (`keysNodup`, below).

---

**`getCoin`.** For a UTXO set $u$ and an outpoint $p$, $\mathrm{getCoin}(u, p)$ is an optional coin defined by recursion on the list: if $u$ is empty the result is "none"; if $u = (k, c) :: \mathrm{rest}$ then the result is "some $c$" when $k = p$, and otherwise $\mathrm{getCoin}(\mathrm{rest}, p)$. So the result is the coin of the *first* (left-most) entry whose outpoint equals $p$, or "none" if no entry has outpoint $p$; later entries with the same outpoint are ignored. I write $u[p]$ for $\mathrm{getCoin}(u,p)$.

---

**`haveCoin`.** For a UTXO set $u$ and outpoint $p$, $\mathrm{haveCoin}(u, p)$ is the Boolean that is true exactly when $u[p]$ is "some coin", i.e. when at least one entry of $u$ has outpoint $p$.

---

**`keysNodup`.** For a UTXO set $u$, $\mathrm{keysNodup}(u)$ is the proposition that the list of first components of $u$ (the outpoints, in order, with multiplicity) has no duplicate element, i.e. the outpoints of $u$ are pairwise distinct. It says nothing about the coins. The empty list satisfies it.

---

**`spendCoin`.** For a UTXO set $u$ and outpoint $p$, $\mathrm{spendCoin}(u, p)$ is the UTXO set obtained by recursion: the empty list maps to the empty list; $(k, c) :: \mathrm{rest}$ maps to $\mathrm{spendCoin}(\mathrm{rest}, p)$ if $k = p$, and to $(k, c) :: \mathrm{spendCoin}(\mathrm{rest}, p)$ otherwise. Thus *every* entry whose outpoint equals $p$ is removed (not only the first), the relative order of the remaining entries is preserved, and if no entry has outpoint $p$ the list is returned unchanged. There is no failure case when $p$ is absent.

---

**`addCoin`.** For a UTXO set $u$, outpoint $p$ and coin $c$:
$$\mathrm{addCoin}(u, p, c) = \begin{cases} u & \text{if } c.\mathrm{out}.\mathrm{unspendable} = \mathrm{true},\\ (p, c) :: \mathrm{spendCoin}(u, p) & \text{otherwise.}\end{cases}$$
In the unspendable case $u$ is returned *unchanged* — in particular any existing entry at outpoint $p$ is kept. In the spendable case all existing entries at outpoint $p$ are first removed and the new pair $(p, c)$ is placed at the *front* of the list (replace-on-insert).

---

**`addCoinsFrom`.** Given a transaction id $t \in T$, a height $h \in \mathbb{N}$, a Boolean $\mathrm{cb}$, a UTXO set $u$, a starting index $i \in \mathbb{N}$ and a list of outputs: if the list is empty the result is $u$; if it is $o :: \mathrm{rest}$, the result is
$$\mathrm{addCoinsFrom}\big(t, h, \mathrm{cb},\ \mathrm{addCoin}(u, \langle t, i\rangle, \langle o, h, \mathrm{cb}\rangle),\ i + 1,\ \mathrm{rest}\big),$$
where $\langle o, h, \mathrm{cb}\rangle$ is the coin with output $o$, height $h$ and coinbase flag $\mathrm{cb}$. So the $k$-th output of the list (counting from $0$) is added at outpoint $\langle t, i + k\rangle$, left to right, each insertion applied to the result of the previous one. An unspendable output still consumes its index (the index advances to $i+1$ whether or not anything was inserted).

---

**`spendInputs`.** For a UTXO set $u$ and a list of outpoints: the empty list gives $u$; $p :: \mathrm{rest}$ gives $\mathrm{spendInputs}(\mathrm{spendCoin}(u, p), \mathrm{rest})$. That is, $\mathrm{spendCoin}$ is applied successively for each outpoint in the list, in order. Outpoints absent from $u$, or repeated in the list, cause no error.

---

**`updateCoins`.** For a UTXO set $u$, a transaction $\mathrm{tx}$ and a height $h \in \mathbb{N}$:
$$\mathrm{updateCoins}(u, \mathrm{tx}, h) = \mathrm{addCoinsFrom}\big(\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{txid},\ h,\ \mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{isCoinbase},\ u_0,\ 0,\ \mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vout}\big),$$
where $u_0 = u$ if $\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{isCoinbase} = \mathrm{true}$ and $u_0 = \mathrm{spendInputs}(u, \mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vin})$ otherwise. So for a transaction flagged coinbase the inputs in $\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vin}$ are *not* removed (whatever that list contains), and in both cases the outputs are added at outpoints $\langle \mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{txid}, 0\rangle, \langle \mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{txid}, 1\rangle, \dots$ as coins of height $h$ carrying the transaction's coinbase flag.

---

**`outputsLoop`.** Given a list of outputs and an accumulator $a \in \mathbb{Z}$, the result is an optional integer: the empty list gives "some $a$"; for $o :: \mathrm{rest}$,
- if $o.\mathrm{value} < 0$ the result is "none";
- else if $\mathrm{MAX\_MONEY} < o.\mathrm{value}$ (strict) the result is "none";
- else if $\mathrm{moneyRange}(a + o.\mathrm{value}) = \mathrm{false}$ (i.e. not $0 \le a + o.\mathrm{value} \le \mathrm{MAX\_MONEY}$) the result is "none";
- else the result is $\mathrm{outputsLoop}(\mathrm{rest}, a + o.\mathrm{value})$.

So it returns "some $a + \sum o.\mathrm{value}$" exactly when every output value lies in $[0, \mathrm{MAX\_MONEY}]$ and every partial sum $a + (\text{values so far})$ lies in $[0, \mathrm{MAX\_MONEY}]$; on an empty list it returns "some $a$" without any test.

---

**`sumValues`.** For a list of outputs, $\mathrm{sumValues}([\,]) = 0$ and $\mathrm{sumValues}(o :: \mathrm{rest}) = o.\mathrm{value} + \mathrm{sumValues}(\mathrm{rest})$: the integer sum of the values, with no range check.

---

**`valueOut`.** For a transaction $\mathrm{tx}$, $\mathrm{valueOut}(\mathrm{tx}) = \mathrm{sumValues}(\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vout}) = \sum_{o \in \mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vout}} o.\mathrm{value} \in \mathbb{Z}$ (zero for an empty output list).

---

**`valueIn`.** For a UTXO set $u$ and a list of outpoints: $\mathrm{valueIn}(u, [\,]) = 0$, and
$$\mathrm{valueIn}(u, p :: \mathrm{rest}) = \big(\text{if } u[p] = \text{none then } 0 \text{ else } c.\mathrm{out}.\mathrm{value} \text{ where } u[p] = \text{some } c\big) + \mathrm{valueIn}(u, \mathrm{rest}).$$
So it is the sum, with multiplicity over the list, of the values of the first-matching coins, contributing $0$ for an outpoint with no entry in $u$. A repeated outpoint is counted once per occurrence.

---

**`checkTransaction`.** For a transaction $\mathrm{tx}$, the Boolean conjunction of four conditions:
1. $\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vin}$ is non-empty;
2. $\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vout}$ is non-empty;
3. $\mathrm{outputsLoop}(\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vout}, 0)$ is "some $\cdot$" (every output value in $[0,\mathrm{MAX\_MONEY}]$ and every partial sum from $0$ in $[0, \mathrm{MAX\_MONEY}]$);
4. the list $\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vin}$ has no duplicate outpoints.

It does not inspect $\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{isCoinbase}$ or $\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{txid}$.

---

**`haveInputs`.** For a UTXO set $u$ and a transaction $\mathrm{tx}$: $\mathrm{haveInputs}(u, \mathrm{tx}) = \mathrm{true}$ iff $\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{isCoinbase} = \mathrm{true}$, or every outpoint $p$ in $\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vin}$ satisfies $\mathrm{haveCoin}(u, p) = \mathrm{true}$. For a coinbase-flagged transaction it is true regardless of $\mathrm{vin}$; for an empty $\mathrm{vin}$ it is true vacuously.

---

**`inputsLoop`.** Given a UTXO set $u$, a spend height $s \in \mathbb{N}$, a list of outpoints and an accumulator $a \in \mathbb{Z}$, the result is an optional integer: the empty list gives "some $a$"; for $p :: \mathrm{rest}$,
- if $u[p] = $ none, the result is "none";
- if $u[p] = $ some $\mathrm{coin}$: if $\mathrm{coin}.\mathrm{isCoinbase} = \mathrm{true}$ and $s \mathbin{\dot-} \mathrm{coin}.\mathrm{height} < 100$, the result is "none", where $\dot-$ is *truncated* natural-number subtraction ($x \dot- y = 0$ whenever $x \le y$); consequently a coinbase coin with $\mathrm{coin}.\mathrm{height} \ge s$ has $s \dot- \mathrm{coin}.\mathrm{height} = 0 < 100$ and is rejected, and a coinbase coin passes exactly when $s \ge \mathrm{coin}.\mathrm{height} + 100$; a non-coinbase coin is never rejected by this test;
- otherwise let $a' = a + \mathrm{coin}.\mathrm{out}.\mathrm{value}$; if $\mathrm{moneyRange}(\mathrm{coin}.\mathrm{out}.\mathrm{value}) = \mathrm{false}$ or $\mathrm{moneyRange}(a') = \mathrm{false}$, the result is "none"; else the result is $\mathrm{inputsLoop}(u, s, \mathrm{rest}, a')$.

A repeated outpoint in the list is processed (and its value added) once per occurrence.

---

**`checkTxInputs`.** For a UTXO set $u$, a transaction $\mathrm{tx}$ and a spend height $s \in \mathbb{N}$, an optional integer:
- if $\mathrm{haveInputs}(u, \mathrm{tx}) = \mathrm{false}$, "none";
- else if $\mathrm{inputsLoop}(u, s, \mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vin}, 0) = $ none, "none";
- else, with $\mathrm{inputsLoop}(u, s, \mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vin}, 0) = $ some $v_{\mathrm{in}}$ and $v_{\mathrm{out}} = \mathrm{valueOut}(\mathrm{tx})$: if $v_{\mathrm{in}} < v_{\mathrm{out}}$, "none"; else let $\mathrm{fee} = v_{\mathrm{in}} - v_{\mathrm{out}}$; if $\mathrm{moneyRange}(\mathrm{fee}) = \mathrm{false}$, "none"; otherwise "some $\mathrm{fee}$".

Note that even for a coinbase-flagged transaction (for which $\mathrm{haveInputs}$ is automatically true) the loop still requires every outpoint of $\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vin}$ to be present in $u$; with an empty $\mathrm{vin}$ the loop yields $v_{\mathrm{in}} = 0$.

---

**`bip30Ok`.** For a UTXO set $u$ and a list of transactions $B$: the Boolean that is true iff for every transaction $\mathrm{tx}$ in $B$ (including any coinbase) and every index $o \in \{0, 1, \dots, |\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vout}| - 1\}$, $\mathrm{haveCoin}(u, \langle \mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{txid}, o\rangle) = \mathrm{false}$. It is tested against the single set $u$ given, not against intermediate states; it is vacuously true for an empty block or for a transaction with no outputs, and it does not look at indices $\ge |\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vout}|$.

---

**`checkBlockTxs`.** For a list of transactions: the empty list gives $\mathrm{false}$; $\mathrm{cb} :: \mathrm{rest}$ gives the conjunction of $\mathrm{cb}.\mathrm{isCoinbase} = \mathrm{true}$, $\mathrm{checkTransaction}(\mathrm{cb}) = \mathrm{true}$, and, for every $\mathrm{tx}$ in $\mathrm{rest}$, $\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{isCoinbase} = \mathrm{false}$ and $\mathrm{checkTransaction}(\mathrm{tx}) = \mathrm{true}$. A block consisting of the coinbase alone passes if the coinbase passes `checkTransaction` (which in particular requires it to have at least one input and one output).

---

**`connectLoop`.** Given a height $h \in \mathbb{N}$, a UTXO set $u$, an accumulated fee $f \in \mathbb{Z}$ and a list of transactions, the result is an optional pair (UTXO set, integer): the empty list gives "some $(u, f)$"; for $\mathrm{tx} :: \mathrm{rest}$,
- if $\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{isCoinbase} = \mathrm{true}$, the result is $\mathrm{connectLoop}(h, \mathrm{updateCoins}(u, \mathrm{tx}, h), f, \mathrm{rest})$ — no input check and no fee change, wherever in the list such a transaction sits;
- otherwise, if $\mathrm{checkTxInputs}(u, \mathrm{tx}, h) = $ none, "none"; if it is some $\mathrm{fee}$, let $f' = f + \mathrm{fee}$; if $\mathrm{moneyRange}(f') = \mathrm{false}$, "none"; else $\mathrm{connectLoop}(h, \mathrm{updateCoins}(u, \mathrm{tx}, h), f', \mathrm{rest})$.

The same $h$ is used both as the spend height passed to `checkTxInputs` and as the creation height of the new coins.

---

**`connectBlock`.** Given a function $\mathrm{subsidy} : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$, a UTXO set $u$, a height $h \in \mathbb{N}$ and a list of transactions $B$, an optional pair (UTXO set, integer):
- if $\mathrm{checkBlockTxs}(B) = \mathrm{false}$, "none";
- else if $\mathrm{bip30Ok}(u, B) = \mathrm{false}$, "none";
- else if $\mathrm{connectLoop}(h, u, 0, B) = $ none, "none";
- else, with $\mathrm{connectLoop}(h, u, 0, B) = $ some $(u', f)$: if $B$ is empty, "none" (this branch cannot actually occur since `checkBlockTxs` already rejected the empty list, but it is what the code returns); if $B = \mathrm{cb} :: \_$, then "none" if $\mathrm{valueOut}(\mathrm{cb}) > f + \mathrm{subsidy}(h)$ (strict), and "some $(u', f)$" otherwise, i.e. when $\mathrm{valueOut}(\mathrm{cb}) \le f + \mathrm{subsidy}(h)$.

Only the first transaction's output value is compared against $f + \mathrm{subsidy}(h)$; $\mathrm{subsidy}(h)$ may be any integer, including negative.

---

**`connectChain`.** Given $\mathrm{subsidy} : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$, a UTXO set $u$, a height $h \in \mathbb{N}$ and a list of blocks (each a list of transactions), an optional UTXO set: the empty list of blocks gives "some $u$"; $B :: \mathrm{rest}$ gives "none" if $\mathrm{connectBlock}(\mathrm{subsidy}, u, h, B) = $ none, and otherwise, with that result some $(u', \_)$, gives $\mathrm{connectChain}(\mathrm{subsidy}, u', h + 1, \mathrm{rest})$. The fee component returned by each block is discarded; the $k$-th block (from $0$) is connected at height $h + k$.

---

**`totalValue`.** For a UTXO set $u$: $\mathrm{totalValue}([\,]) = 0$ and $\mathrm{totalValue}((\_, c) :: \mathrm{rest}) = c.\mathrm{out}.\mathrm{value} + \mathrm{totalValue}(\mathrm{rest})$: the integer sum of the values of *all* entries, counted with multiplicity even if several entries share an outpoint, with no range check. I write it $\mathrm{tv}(u)$.

---

**`subsidySum`.** For $\mathrm{subsidy} : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$, $h \in \mathbb{N}$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$: $\mathrm{subsidySum}(\mathrm{subsidy}, h, 0) = 0$ and $\mathrm{subsidySum}(\mathrm{subsidy}, h, n+1) = \mathrm{subsidySum}(\mathrm{subsidy}, h, n) + \mathrm{subsidy}(h + n)$, i.e.
$$\mathrm{subsidySum}(\mathrm{subsidy}, h, n) = \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} \mathrm{subsidy}(h + k) \in \mathbb{Z},$$
which is $0$ for $n = 0$.

theorem BitcoinUtxo.checkTransaction_outputs {T : Type} [DecidableEq T] (tx : Tx T) (h : checkTransaction tx = true) :

**Read-back of `BitcoinUtxo.checkTransaction_outputs`.**

Let $T$ be any type with decidable equality. A *transaction* $\mathrm{tx}$ over $T$ is a record with a transaction id $\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{txid} \in T$, a finite list of inputs $\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vin}$ (each an outpoint: a transaction id in $T$ together with an index in $\mathbb{N}$), a finite list of outputs $\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vout}$ (each an output record $o$ with an integer $o.\mathrm{value} \in \mathbb{Z}$ and a Boolean $o.\mathrm{unspendable}$), and an independent Boolean flag $\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{isCoinbase}$. The constant $\mathrm{MAX\_MONEY}$ is the integer $21{,}000{,}000 \times 10^8 = 2.1 \times 10^{15}$, and $\mathrm{moneyRange}(v)$ is the Boolean "$0 \le v \le \mathrm{MAX\_MONEY}$".

The Boolean $\mathrm{checkTransaction}(\mathrm{tx})$ is the conjunction of:

1. $\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vin}$ is non-empty;
2. $\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vout}$ is non-empty;
3. the output loop started at accumulator $0$ succeeds: walking through $\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vout} = [o_1, \dots, o_k]$ in order with running total $a_0 = 0$, $a_j = a_{j-1} + o_j.\mathrm{value}$, no step fails, where step $j$ fails if $o_j.\mathrm{value} < 0$, or if $\mathrm{MAX\_MONEY} < o_j.\mathrm{value}$, or if $\mathrm{moneyRange}(a_j) = \mathrm{false}$ (i.e. not $0 \le a_j \le \mathrm{MAX\_MONEY}$);
4. the list $\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vin}$ has no duplicate entries.

The theorem states: for every type $T$ with decidable equality and every transaction $\mathrm{tx}$ over $T$, **if** $\mathrm{checkTransaction}(\mathrm{tx}) = \mathrm{true}$, **then**

- the list $\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vin}$ has no duplicate outpoints, **and**
- for every output $o$ occurring in $\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vout}$, $0 \le o.\mathrm{value}$ and $o.\mathrm{value} \le \mathrm{MAX\_MONEY}$ (both inequalities non-strict).

The conclusion says nothing about the non-emptiness of $\mathrm{vin}$ or $\mathrm{vout}$, nothing about the partial sums or the total $\sum o.\mathrm{value}$ being at most $\mathrm{MAX\_MONEY}$, and nothing about $\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{isCoinbase}$ or $\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{txid}$, even though some of these are tested by the hypothesis. The universal statement over outputs is vacuous if $\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vout}$ were empty, but the hypothesis rules that out.

items.theorem_title: CheckTxInputs returns the fee, in range, with all inputs present
items.formal_statement:
theorem BitcoinUtxo.checkTxInputs_some {T : Type} [DecidableEq T] (u : UtxoSet T) (tx : Tx T) (h : Nat) (fee : Int)
    (hfee : checkTxInputs u tx h = some fee) :
    fee = valueIn u tx.vin - valueOut tx ∧ 0 ≤ fee ∧ fee ≤ MAX_MONEY ∧
    ∀ op ∈ tx.vin, haveCoin u op = true := by sorry
items.natural_language_statement:
For every view $U$, transaction $tx$, spend height $h$ and amount $f$ with $\mathrm{checkTxInputs}(U, tx, h) = \mathrm{some}(f)$:
$$f = \mathrm{valueIn}(U, tx.\mathrm{vin}) - \mathrm{valueOut}(tx), \qquad 0 \le f \le \mathrm{MAX\_MONEY},$$
and every input outpoint of $tx$ is present in $U$. The fee returned through `txfee` is exactly the difference of input and output values, and the input loop guarantees that every input it summed exists.

**Read-back of `BitcoinUtxo.checkTxInputs_some`.**

Let $T$ be any type with decidable equality. A *UTXO set* $u$ over $T$ is a finite ordered list of pairs (outpoint, coin), where an outpoint is $\langle \mathrm{txid}, n\rangle$ with $\mathrm{txid} \in T$, $n \in \mathbb{N}$, and a coin $c$ is a record with an output $c.\mathrm{out}$ (an integer $c.\mathrm{out}.\mathrm{value}$ and a Boolean $c.\mathrm{out}.\mathrm{unspendable}$), a height $c.\mathrm{height} \in \mathbb{N}$ and a Boolean $c.\mathrm{isCoinbase}$. Write $u[p]$ for the coin of the first entry of $u$ with outpoint $p$ (or "none"), and $\mathrm{haveCoin}(u, p)$ for the Boolean "$u[p]$ is not none". A *transaction* $\mathrm{tx}$ has fields $\mathrm{txid} \in T$, $\mathrm{vin}$ (a list of outpoints), $\mathrm{vout}$ (a list of outputs) and a Boolean $\mathrm{isCoinbase}$. Let $\mathrm{MAX\_MONEY} = 2.1 \times 10^{15}$ and $\mathrm{moneyRange}(v) \iff 0 \le v \le \mathrm{MAX\_MONEY}$. Set
$$\mathrm{valueOut}(\mathrm{tx}) = \sum_{o \in \mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vout}} o.\mathrm{value}, \qquad \mathrm{valueIn}(u, \mathrm{ops}) = \sum_{p \in \mathrm{ops}} \begin{cases} c.\mathrm{out}.\mathrm{value} & u[p] = \text{some } c\\ 0 & u[p] = \text{none}\end{cases}$$
(both sums over the lists with multiplicity; $0$ for empty lists).

The function $\mathrm{checkTxInputs}(u, \mathrm{tx}, h)$, for a spend height $h \in \mathbb{N}$, returns an optional integer as follows.

- If $\mathrm{haveInputs}(u, \mathrm{tx})$ is false, i.e. $\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{isCoinbase} = \mathrm{false}$ and some $p \in \mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vin}$ has $\mathrm{haveCoin}(u, p) = \mathrm{false}$: none.
- Otherwise run the input loop over $\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vin} = [p_1, \dots, p_m]$ with accumulator $a_0 = 0$: at step $i$, if $u[p_i] = $ none, fail; if $u[p_i] = $ some $c_i$ and $c_i.\mathrm{isCoinbase} = \mathrm{true}$ and $h \mathbin{\dot-} c_i.\mathrm{height} < 100$ (truncated natural subtraction, so this holds in particular whenever $c_i.\mathrm{height} \ge h$), fail; else set $a_i = a_{i-1} + c_i.\mathrm{out}.\mathrm{value}$ and fail if $\mathrm{moneyRange}(c_i.\mathrm{out}.\mathrm{value})$ is false or $\mathrm{moneyRange}(a_i)$ is false. If any step fails: none. Otherwise $v_{\mathrm{in}} = a_m$ (which equals $\mathrm{valueIn}(u, \mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vin})$, since every $u[p_i]$ is some coin).
- Let $v_{\mathrm{out}} = \mathrm{valueOut}(\mathrm{tx})$. If $v_{\mathrm{in}} < v_{\mathrm{out}}$: none. Else let $\mathrm{fee} = v_{\mathrm{in}} - v_{\mathrm{out}}$; if $\mathrm{moneyRange}(\mathrm{fee})$ is false: none; else some $\mathrm{fee}$.

The theorem states: for every type $T$ with decidable equality, every UTXO set $u$ over $T$, every transaction $\mathrm{tx}$ over $T$, every height $h \in \mathbb{N}$ and every integer $\mathrm{fee}$, **if** $\mathrm{checkTxInputs}(u, \mathrm{tx}, h) = \text{some } \mathrm{fee}$, **then** all four of the following hold:

1. $\mathrm{fee} = \mathrm{valueIn}(u, \mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vin}) - \mathrm{valueOut}(\mathrm{tx})$ (exact integer equality);
2. $0 \le \mathrm{fee}$;
3. $\mathrm{fee} \le \mathrm{MAX\_MONEY}$;
4. for every outpoint $p$ occurring in $\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vin}$, $\mathrm{haveCoin}(u, p) = \mathrm{true}$.

There is no hypothesis that the outpoints of $u$ are distinct, none that $\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vin}$ has no duplicates (a repeated input contributes its coin's value once per occurrence both in the loop and in $\mathrm{valueIn}$), and no hypothesis on $\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{isCoinbase}$: a coinbase-flagged transaction is covered too, and for it conclusion 4 still follows because the input loop itself requires every $u[p_i]$ to be present. If $\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vin}$ is empty, conclusion 4 is vacuous and $\mathrm{valueIn} = 0$. The conclusion does not mention the maturity test or the individual coin-value range tests, though the hypothesis entails them.

items.theorem_title: Spending a present coin removes exactly its value
items.formal_statement:
theorem BitcoinUtxo.totalValue_spend {T : Type} [DecidableEq T] (u : UtxoSet T) (op : OutPoint T) (c : Coin)
    (hn : keysNodup u) (h : getCoin u op = some c) :
    totalValue (spendCoin u op) = totalValue u - c.out.value := by sorry
items.natural_language_statement:
For every view $U$ with pairwise distinct outpoints, outpoint $p$ and coin $c$ with $\mathrm{getCoin}(U, p) = \mathrm{some}(c)$,
$$\mathrm{totalValue}(\mathrm{spendCoin}(U, p)) = \mathrm{totalValue}(U) - c.\mathrm{value}.$$
Distinctness is what makes the removed entry unique.

**Read-back of `BitcoinUtxo.totalValue_spend`.**

Let $T$ be any type with decidable equality. A *UTXO set* $u$ over $T$ is a finite ordered list of pairs $(p, c)$, where $p = \langle \mathrm{txid}, n\rangle$ is an outpoint (a transaction id in $T$ together with an index $n \in \mathbb{N}$) and $c$ is a coin, i.e. a record consisting of an output $c.\mathrm{out}$ (an integer $c.\mathrm{out}.\mathrm{value} \in \mathbb{Z}$ and a Boolean $c.\mathrm{out}.\mathrm{unspendable}$), a height $c.\mathrm{height} \in \mathbb{N}$ and a Boolean $c.\mathrm{isCoinbase}$. Write $u[p]$ for the lookup that returns the coin of the *first* entry of $u$ whose outpoint equals $p$, or "none" if there is no such entry. Write $\mathrm{tv}(u)$ for the *total value* of $u$: the integer sum of $c.\mathrm{out}.\mathrm{value}$ over every entry $(p, c)$ of the list, counting each entry (with multiplicity, even for repeated outpoints) and with no range restriction; $\mathrm{tv}([\,]) = 0$. Write $\mathrm{spendCoin}(u, p)$ for the list obtained from $u$ by deleting *every* entry whose outpoint equals $p$, keeping the others in order (if no entry matches, the list is unchanged). Write $\mathrm{keysNodup}(u)$ for the proposition that the list of outpoints of $u$ (first components, in order) contains no duplicates.

The theorem states: for every type $T$ with decidable equality, every UTXO set $u$ over $T$, every outpoint $p$ over $T$ and every coin $c$, **if**

- $\mathrm{keysNodup}(u)$ holds (the outpoints of $u$ are pairwise distinct), and
- $u[p] = \text{some } c$ (the first — hence, under the previous hypothesis, the only — entry of $u$ with outpoint $p$ carries exactly the coin $c$),

**then**
$$\mathrm{tv}\big(\mathrm{spendCoin}(u, p)\big) = \mathrm{tv}(u) - c.\mathrm{out}.\mathrm{value},$$
an equality of integers (ordinary subtraction in $\mathbb{Z}$, no truncation). The conclusion is an exact equality, not an inequality. The hypotheses exclude the case where $p$ is absent from $u$ (then $u[p]$ would be "none"), so $u$ is non-empty whenever the hypotheses hold. No constraint is placed on the sign or magnitude of $c.\mathrm{out}.\mathrm{value}$ or of any other value in $u$, nor on $c.\mathrm{out}.\mathrm{unspendable}$, $c.\mathrm{height}$ or $c.\mathrm{isCoinbase}$.

theorem BitcoinUtxo.totalValue_add_fresh {T : Type} [DecidableEq T] (u : UtxoSet T) (op : OutPoint T) (c : Coin)
    (h : getCoin u op = none) :
    totalValue (addCoin u op c) = totalValue u + (if c.out.unspendable then 0 else c.out.value) := by sorry
items.natural_language_statement:
For every view $U$, outpoint $p$ absent from $U$, and coin $c$,
$$\mathrm{totalValue}(\mathrm{addCoin}(U, p, c)) = \mathrm{totalValue}(U) + \begin{cases} 0 & c \text{ unspendable} \\ c.\mathrm{value} & \text{otherwise.}\end{cases}$$

theorem BitcoinUtxo.totalValue_spendInputs {T : Type} [DecidableEq T] (u : UtxoSet T) :
    ∀ (ops : List (OutPoint T)), keysNodup u → ops.Nodup → (∀ op ∈ ops, haveCoin u op = true) →

$$\mathrm{totalValue}(\mathrm{spendInputs}(U, I)) = \mathrm{totalValue}(U) - \mathrm{valueIn}(U, I).$$
Without distinctness of $I$ the identity fails: a repeated outpoint is counted twice in `valueIn` but removed once.

the sum being over the list with multiplicity and equal to $0$ for the empty list.

The theorem states: for every type $T$ with decidable equality and every UTXO set $u$ over $T$, **for every** finite list $\mathrm{ops}$ of outpoints over $T$, **if**

- $\mathrm{keysNodup}(u)$ (the outpoints of $u$ are pairwise distinct), and
- the list $\mathrm{ops}$ has no duplicate outpoints (as a list over the outpoint type, i.e. no two positions hold the same pair $\langle \mathrm{txid}, n\rangle$), and
- for every outpoint $p$ occurring in $\mathrm{ops}$, $\mathrm{haveCoin}(u, p) = \mathrm{true}$ (every listed outpoint has an entry in $u$),

**then**
$$\mathrm{tv}\big(\mathrm{spendInputs}(u, \mathrm{ops})\big) = \mathrm{tv}(u) - \mathrm{valueIn}(u, \mathrm{ops}),$$
an exact equality in $\mathbb{Z}$.

The quantifier over $\mathrm{ops}$ is inside the statement, after $u$ is fixed; $\mathrm{ops}$ may be empty, in which case the third hypothesis is vacuous and the conclusion reads $\mathrm{tv}(u) = \mathrm{tv}(u) - 0$. No sign or range condition is imposed on any coin value.

items.theorem_title: An accepted ordinary transaction cannot create value
items.formal_statement:
theorem BitcoinUtxo.tx_conservation {T : Type} [DecidableEq T] (u : UtxoSet T) (tx : Tx T) (h : Nat) (fee : Int)
    (hn : keysNodup u) (hnd : tx.vin.Nodup) (hcb : tx.isCoinbase = false)
    (hfee : checkTxInputs u tx h = some fee)
    (hfresh : ∀ j, j < tx.vout.length → getCoin u ⟨tx.txid, j⟩ = none)
    (hpos : ∀ o ∈ tx.vout, 0 ≤ o.value) :
    totalValue (updateCoins u tx h) ≤ totalValue u - fee := by sorry
items.natural_language_statement:
For every view $U$ with distinct outpoints, non-coinbase transaction $tx$ with distinct inputs, spend height $h$ and fee $f$ such that $\mathrm{checkTxInputs}(U, tx, h) = \mathrm{some}(f)$, provided no outpoint $(tx.\mathrm{txid}, j)$ with $j < |tx.\mathrm{vout}|$ is present in $U$ and every output value is non-negative,
$$\mathrm{totalValue}(\mathrm{updateCoins}(U, tx, h)) \le \mathrm{totalValue}(U) - f.$$
The ledger loses the fee, and loses more when an output is unspendable. The freshness hypothesis is the BIP30 condition; non-negativity of the outputs comes from `CheckTransaction`.

items.theorem_title: A coinbase adds at most its output value
items.formal_statement:
theorem BitcoinUtxo.coinbase_bound {T : Type} [DecidableEq T] (u : UtxoSet T) (tx : Tx T) (h : Nat)
    (hcb : tx.isCoinbase = true)
    (hfresh : ∀ j, j < tx.vout.length → getCoin u ⟨tx.txid, j⟩ = none)
    (hpos : ∀ o ∈ tx.vout, 0 ≤ o.value) :
    totalValue (updateCoins u tx h) ≤ totalValue u + valueOut tx := by sorry
items.natural_language_statement:
For every view $U$, coinbase transaction $tx$, height $h$, provided no outpoint $(tx.\mathrm{txid}, j)$ with $j < |tx.\mathrm{vout}|$ is present in $U$ and every output value is non-negative,
$$\mathrm{totalValue}(\mathrm{updateCoins}(U, tx, h)) \le \mathrm{totalValue}(U) + \mathrm{valueOut}(tx).$$
Equality holds when no output is unspendable.

items.readback:
**Read-back of `BitcoinUtxo.coinbase_bound`.**

Let $T$ be any type with decidable equality. A *UTXO set* $u$ over $T$ is a finite ordered list of pairs (outpoint, coin): an outpoint is $\langle \mathrm{txid}, n\rangle$ with $\mathrm{txid} \in T$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$; a coin $c$ has an output $c.\mathrm{out}$ (an integer $c.\mathrm{out}.\mathrm{value}$ and a Boolean $c.\mathrm{out}.\mathrm{unspendable}$), a height $c.\mathrm{height} \in \mathbb{N}$ and a Boolean $c.\mathrm{isCoinbase}$. $u[p]$ is the coin of the first entry of $u$ with outpoint $p$, or "none". $\mathrm{tv}(u)$ is the integer sum of $c.\mathrm{out}.\mathrm{value}$ over all entries of $u$ (with multiplicity, no range restriction). A *transaction* $\mathrm{tx}$ has fields $\mathrm{txid} \in T$, $\mathrm{vin}$ (a list of outpoints), $\mathrm{vout}$ (a list of outputs $o$ with integer $o.\mathrm{value}$ and Boolean $o.\mathrm{unspendable}$) and Boolean $\mathrm{isCoinbase}$; $\mathrm{valueOut}(\mathrm{tx}) = \sum_{o \in \mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vout}} o.\mathrm{value}$ (zero if $\mathrm{vout}$ is empty).

$\mathrm{spendCoin}(u, p)$ deletes every entry of outpoint $p$ from $u$. $\mathrm{addCoin}(u, p, c)$ is $u$ unchanged if $c.\mathrm{out}.\mathrm{unspendable} = \mathrm{true}$, and otherwise $(p, c)$ prepended to $\mathrm{spendCoin}(u, p)$. For a transaction with $\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{isCoinbase} = \mathrm{true}$ (the case of this theorem), the inputs are *not* spent, and
$$\mathrm{updateCoins}(u, \mathrm{tx}, h) = \text{the result of successively applying } \mathrm{addCoin}\big(\cdot, \langle \mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{txid}, j\rangle, \langle o_j, h, \mathrm{true}\rangle\big) \text{ to } u \text{ for } j = 0, 1, \dots, |\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vout}|-1,$$
where $o_j$ is the $j$-th output of $\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vout}$ and $\langle o_j, h, \mathrm{true}\rangle$ is the coin with output $o_j$, height $h$ and coinbase flag true. An unspendable output adds nothing but still consumes its index.

The theorem states: for every type $T$ with decidable equality, every UTXO set $u$ over $T$, every transaction $\mathrm{tx}$ over $T$ and every height $h \in \mathbb{N}$, **if**

- $\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{isCoinbase} = \mathrm{true}$;
- (freshness) for every natural number $j < |\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vout}|$, $u[\langle \mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{txid}, j\rangle] = \text{none}$, i.e. $u$ has no entry at any of the outpoints $\langle \mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{txid}, 0\rangle, \dots, \langle \mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{txid}, |\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vout}|-1\rangle$ (indices $\ge |\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vout}|$ are not covered; vacuous when $\mathrm{vout}$ is empty);
- for every output $o$ occurring in $\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vout}$, $0 \le o.\mathrm{value}$;

**then**
$$\mathrm{tv}\big(\mathrm{updateCoins}(u, \mathrm{tx}, h)\big) \le \mathrm{tv}(u) + \mathrm{valueOut}(\mathrm{tx}),$$
a non-strict integer inequality.

There is **no** hypothesis that the outpoints of $u$ are pairwise distinct, no hypothesis that $\mathrm{tx}$ passes `checkTransaction` or any input check, no upper bound on the output values, and no constraint on $\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vin}$ (which plays no role, since a coinbase-flagged transaction spends nothing). The height $h$ enters only as the recorded height of the newly added coins and does not affect the conclusion's quantities.

items.theorem_title: An accepted block raises the ledger by at most the subsidy
items.formal_statement:
theorem BitcoinUtxo.block_bound {T : Type} [DecidableEq T] (subsidy : Nat → Int) (u : UtxoSet T) (h : Nat) (block : List (Tx T))
    (u' : UtxoSet T) (fees : Int) (hn : keysNodup u) (hnd : (block.map Tx.txid).Nodup)
    (hc : connectBlock subsidy u h block = some (u', fees)) :
    totalValue u' ≤ totalValue u + subsidy h ∧ keysNodup u' := by sorry
items.natural_language_statement:
For every subsidy function $s$, view $U$ with distinct outpoints, height $h$, and block $B$ whose transactions have pairwise distinct txids, if $\mathrm{connectBlock}_s(U, h, B) = \mathrm{some}(U', \mathrm{fees})$ then
$$\mathrm{totalValue}(U') \le \mathrm{totalValue}(U) + s(h),$$
and $U'$ has pairwise distinct outpoints. The fees paid by the block's transactions leave the ledger and are returned to it by the coinbase, which may add at most $s(h)$ beyond them.

**Read-back of `BitcoinUtxo.block_bound`.**

Let $T$ be any type with decidable equality. A *UTXO set* over $T$ is a finite ordered list of pairs (outpoint, coin): an outpoint is $\langle \mathrm{txid}, n\rangle$ with $\mathrm{txid} \in T$, $n \in \mathbb{N}$; a coin $c$ has an output $c.\mathrm{out}$ (integer $c.\mathrm{out}.\mathrm{value}$, Boolean $c.\mathrm{out}.\mathrm{unspendable}$), a height $c.\mathrm{height} \in \mathbb{N}$ and a Boolean $c.\mathrm{isCoinbase}$. $u[p]$ is the coin of the first entry of $u$ with outpoint $p$, or "none"; $\mathrm{haveCoin}(u, p)$ is "$u[p]$ is not none". $\mathrm{tv}(u)$ is the integer sum of $c.\mathrm{out}.\mathrm{value}$ over all entries of $u$. $\mathrm{keysNodup}(u)$ is the proposition that the outpoints of $u$ are pairwise distinct. A *transaction* $\mathrm{tx}$ has fields $\mathrm{txid} \in T$, $\mathrm{vin}$ (list of outpoints), $\mathrm{vout}$ (list of outputs $o$ with integer $o.\mathrm{value}$, Boolean $o.\mathrm{unspendable}$), Boolean $\mathrm{isCoinbase}$; $\mathrm{valueOut}(\mathrm{tx}) = \sum_{o \in \mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vout}} o.\mathrm{value}$. A *block* is a finite list of transactions. $\mathrm{MAX\_MONEY} = 2.1\times 10^{15}$, $\mathrm{moneyRange}(v) \iff 0 \le v \le \mathrm{MAX\_MONEY}$.

The function $\mathrm{connectBlock}(\mathrm{subsidy}, u, h, B)$, for $\mathrm{subsidy} : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$, returns an optional pair (UTXO set, integer) and is "some $(u', f)$" exactly when all of the following hold:

1. **Structure** ($\mathrm{checkBlockTxs}$): $B$ is non-empty, $B = \mathrm{cb} :: \mathrm{rest}$, with $\mathrm{cb}.\mathrm{isCoinbase} = \mathrm{true}$, $\mathrm{checkTransaction}(\mathrm{cb}) = \mathrm{true}$, and for every $\mathrm{tx} \in \mathrm{rest}$, $\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{isCoinbase} = \mathrm{false}$ and $\mathrm{checkTransaction}(\mathrm{tx}) = \mathrm{true}$. Here $\mathrm{checkTransaction}(\mathrm{tx})$ means: $\mathrm{vin}$ non-empty, $\mathrm{vout}$ non-empty, every output value in $[0, \mathrm{MAX\_MONEY}]$ with every partial sum (from $0$, in list order) in $[0, \mathrm{MAX\_MONEY}]$, and $\mathrm{vin}$ without duplicates.
2. **BIP30 pre-check** ($\mathrm{bip30Ok}$): for every $\mathrm{tx} \in B$ (the coinbase included) and every index $o \in \{0, \dots, |\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vout}|-1\}$, $\mathrm{haveCoin}(u, \langle \mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{txid}, o\rangle) = \mathrm{false}$, tested against the initial $u$ only.
3. **Transaction loop** ($\mathrm{connectLoop}$ from $(u, 0)$): processing $B$ left to right with current set $w$ (initially $u$) and accumulated fee $f$ (initially $0$): a transaction with $\mathrm{isCoinbase} = \mathrm{true}$ is applied as $w \mapsto \mathrm{updateCoins}(w, \mathrm{tx}, h)$ with $f$ unchanged and no check; a transaction with $\mathrm{isCoinbase} = \mathrm{false}$ requires $\mathrm{checkTxInputs}(w, \mathrm{tx}, h) = \text{some } \mathrm{fee}$ and $\mathrm{moneyRange}(f + \mathrm{fee}) = \mathrm{true}$, then $w \mapsto \mathrm{updateCoins}(w, \mathrm{tx}, h)$, $f \mapsto f + \mathrm{fee}$; the loop yields the final $(u', f)$. Here $\mathrm{updateCoins}(w, \mathrm{tx}, h)$ first (for a non-coinbase transaction only) removes every entry at each outpoint of $\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vin}$, then for $j = 0, \dots, |\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vout}|-1$ in order adds the coin (output $o_j$, height $h$, flag $\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{isCoinbase}$) at $\langle \mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{txid}, j\rangle$ by removing any entry at that outpoint and prepending the new one, unless $o_j.\mathrm{unspendable}$ is true, in which case nothing is added. And $\mathrm{checkTxInputs}(w, \mathrm{tx}, h) = \text{some } \mathrm{fee}$ means: every $p \in \mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vin}$ has $w[p] = $ some coin; for each such coin, not ($c.\mathrm{isCoinbase}$ and $h \mathbin{\dot-} c.\mathrm{height} < 100$, with truncated subtraction); each coin value and each running total of coin values (from $0$, in order, with multiplicity) lies in $[0, \mathrm{MAX\_MONEY}]$; $v_{\mathrm{in}} := $ that total satisfies $v_{\mathrm{in}} \ge \mathrm{valueOut}(\mathrm{tx})$; and $\mathrm{fee} = v_{\mathrm{in}} - \mathrm{valueOut}(\mathrm{tx})$ lies in $[0, \mathrm{MAX\_MONEY}]$.
4. **Coinbase bound**: $\mathrm{valueOut}(\mathrm{cb}) \le f + \mathrm{subsidy}(h)$ (non-strict), where $\mathrm{cb}$ is the first transaction of $B$ and $f$ the final accumulated fee.

The theorem states: for every type $T$ with decidable equality, every function $\mathrm{subsidy} : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$, every UTXO set $u$ over $T$, every height $h \in \mathbb{N}$, every block $B$ of transactions over $T$, every UTXO set $u'$ and every integer $\mathrm{fees}$, **if**

- $\mathrm{keysNodup}(u)$: the outpoints of $u$ are pairwise distinct;
- the list of transaction ids of $B$, $[\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{txid} : \mathrm{tx} \in B]$, has no duplicates (all transactions in the block have pairwise distinct ids);
- $\mathrm{connectBlock}(\mathrm{subsidy}, u, h, B) = \text{some } (u', \mathrm{fees})$;

**then** both

$$\mathrm{tv}(u') \le \mathrm{tv}(u) + \mathrm{subsidy}(h) \qquad\text{and}\qquad \mathrm{keysNodup}(u').$$

The bound involves $\mathrm{subsidy}(h)$ only, not $\mathrm{fees}$; $\mathrm{subsidy}(h)$ may be any integer. The conclusion's inequality is non-strict. No condition is placed on the heights or values of the coins already in $u$ beyond what the success of $\mathrm{connectBlock}$ forces for the coins actually consumed.

items.theorem_title: A chain of accepted blocks raises the ledger by at most the summed subsidies
items.formal_statement:
theorem BitcoinUtxo.chain_bound {T : Type} [DecidableEq T] (subsidy : Nat → Int) :
    ∀ (blocks : List (List (Tx T))) (u : UtxoSet T) (h : Nat) (u' : UtxoSet T),
      keysNodup u → (∀ b ∈ blocks, (b.map Tx.txid).Nodup) →
      connectChain subsidy u h blocks = some u' →
      totalValue u' ≤ totalValue u + subsidySum subsidy h blocks.length := by sorry
items.natural_language_statement:
For every subsidy function $s$, list of blocks $B_1, \dots, B_n$ each with pairwise distinct txids, view $U$ with distinct outpoints and height $h$, if $\mathrm{connectChain}_s(U, h, [B_1, \dots, B_n]) = \mathrm{some}(U')$ then
$$\mathrm{totalValue}(U') \le \mathrm{totalValue}(U) + \sum_{i<n} s(h + i).$$

$$\mathrm{subsidySum}(\mathrm{subsidy}, h, n) = \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} \mathrm{subsidy}(h + k),$$

- $\mathrm{keysNodup}(u)$: the outpoints of $u$ are pairwise distinct;

$$\mathrm{tv}(u') \le \mathrm{tv}(u) + \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} \mathrm{subsidy}(h + k), \qquad n = |\mathrm{blocks}|,$$

For $\mathrm{blocks} = [\,]$ the third hypothesis forces $u' = u$ and the conclusion reads $\mathrm{tv}(u) \le \mathrm{tv}(u) + 0$. items.theorem_title: From an empty ledger, total value never exceeds the subsidies issued
items.formal_statement:
theorem BitcoinUtxo.ledger_bound {T : Type} [DecidableEq T] (subsidy : Nat → Int) (blocks : List (List (Tx T))) (h : Nat)
    (u' : UtxoSet T) (hnd : ∀ b ∈ blocks, (b.map Tx.txid).Nodup)
    (hc : connectChain subsidy [] h blocks = some u') :
    totalValue u' ≤ subsidySum subsidy h blocks.length := by sorry
items.natural_language_statement:
For every subsidy function $s : \mathbb N \to \mathbb Z$, starting height $h$, and sequence of blocks $B_1, \dots, B_n$ whose transactions have pairwise distinct txids within each block, if connecting them from the empty UTXO set succeeds,
$$\mathrm{connectChain}_s([\,], h, [B_1, \dots, B_n]) = \mathrm{some}(U) \;\Longrightarrow\; \mathrm{totalValue}(U) \le \sum_{i<n} s(h + i).$$
Here `connectChain` applies the transcribed `ConnectBlock` accounting — `CheckTransaction`, the BIP30 check, `CheckTxInputs`, fee accumulation, `UpdateCoins`, and the coinbase bound — at consecutive heights.

This is the supply bound of the ledger: fees move value between outputs, unspendable outputs destroy it, and the only creation is the coinbase, bounded by fees plus subsidy. With $s$ the mainnet `GetBlockSubsidy` and $h = 1$ (the genesis coinbase is never connected), the right-hand side is below $\mathrm{MAX\_MONEY}$ by the subsidy mission's bound.

**Formalization Note.** The subsidy is a parameter, so the statement does not depend on the schedule. Distinct txids within a block stand for collision-freedom of transaction hashes, which an abstract id type cannot supply; the BIP30 check is modeled as enforced.

**Read-back of `BitcoinUtxo.ledger_bound`.**

Let $T$ be any type with decidable equality. A *UTXO set* over $T$ is a finite ordered list of pairs (outpoint, coin), where an outpoint is $\langle \mathrm{txid}, n\rangle$ with $\mathrm{txid} \in T$, $n \in \mathbb{N}$, and a coin $c$ carries an output (integer $c.\mathrm{out}.\mathrm{value}$, Boolean $c.\mathrm{out}.\mathrm{unspendable}$), a height $c.\mathrm{height} \in \mathbb{N}$ and a Boolean $c.\mathrm{isCoinbase}$. $w[p]$ denotes the coin of the first entry of $w$ at outpoint $p$, or "none". $\mathrm{tv}(w)$ is the integer sum of $c.\mathrm{out}.\mathrm{value}$ over all entries of $w$, with $\mathrm{tv}([\,]) = 0$. A *transaction* has fields $\mathrm{txid} \in T$, $\mathrm{vin}$ (a list of outpoints), $\mathrm{vout}$ (a list of outputs with integer values and unspendable flags) and a Boolean $\mathrm{isCoinbase}$; a *block* is a list of transactions; $\mathrm{valueOut}(\mathrm{tx})$ is the sum of the output values of $\mathrm{tx}$. $\mathrm{MAX\_MONEY} = 2.1 \times 10^{15}$ and $\mathrm{moneyRange}(v) \iff 0 \le v \le \mathrm{MAX\_MONEY}$.

For $\mathrm{subsidy} : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$, $\mathrm{connectBlock}(\mathrm{subsidy}, w, k, B)$ is "some $(w', f)$" exactly when: (i) $B = \mathrm{cb} :: \mathrm{rest}$ is non-empty, $\mathrm{cb}.\mathrm{isCoinbase}$ is true, every transaction in $\mathrm{rest}$ has $\mathrm{isCoinbase}$ false, and every transaction of $B$ has non-empty $\mathrm{vin}$ and $\mathrm{vout}$, duplicate-free $\mathrm{vin}$, all output values in $[0, \mathrm{MAX\_MONEY}]$ and all partial sums of output values (from $0$, in order) in $[0, \mathrm{MAX\_MONEY}]$; (ii) for every $\mathrm{tx} \in B$ and every $o \in \{0, \dots, |\mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{vout}|-1\}$, $w$ has no entry at $\langle \mathrm{tx}.\mathrm{txid}, o\rangle$; (iii) processing $B$ left to right from $(w, 0)$ succeeds, where a coinbase-flagged transaction is applied without any check or fee change by adding, for $j = 0, \dots, |\mathrm{vout}|-1$, the coin (output $o_j$, height $k$, flag true) at $\langle \mathrm{txid}, j\rangle$ — removing any entry at that outpoint and prepending the new one, or doing nothing if $o_j$ is unspendable — and a non-coinbase transaction requires that every input outpoint have an entry in the current set, that no input coin be a coinbase coin with $k \mathbin{\dot-} \mathrm{height} < 100$ (truncated natural subtraction, so any coinbase coin of height $\ge k$ is rejected), that each input value and each running total of input values be in $[0, \mathrm{MAX\_MONEY}]$, that the input total $v_{\mathrm{in}}$ satisfy $v_{\mathrm{in}} \ge \mathrm{valueOut}(\mathrm{tx})$, that $\mathrm{fee} = v_{\mathrm{in}} - \mathrm{valueOut}(\mathrm{tx}) \in [0, \mathrm{MAX\_MONEY}]$ and that the new accumulated fee $f + \mathrm{fee} \in [0, \mathrm{MAX\_MONEY}]$, after which every entry at each input outpoint is removed and the outputs are added at height $k$ with flag false as above; (iv) $\mathrm{valueOut}(\mathrm{cb}) \le f + \mathrm{subsidy}(k)$ for the final accumulated fee $f$. Then $\mathrm{connectChain}(\mathrm{subsidy}, w_0, h, [B_0, \dots, B_{n-1}])$ is "some $u'$" exactly when there are sets $w_0, w_1, \dots, w_n = u'$ with $\mathrm{connectBlock}(\mathrm{subsidy}, w_i, h + i, B_i) = \text{some } (w_{i+1}, f_i)$ for each $i < n$ (fees discarded); for $n = 0$ it is "some $w_0$". And $\mathrm{subsidySum}(\mathrm{subsidy}, h, n) = \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} \mathrm{subsidy}(h + k)$, equal to $0$ for $n = 0$.

The theorem states: for every type $T$ with decidable equality, every function $\mathrm{subsidy} : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$, every list of blocks $\mathrm{blocks} = [B_0, \dots, B_{n-1}]$ over $T$, every height $h \in \mathbb{N}$ and every UTXO set $u'$ over $T$, **if**

- for every block $B$ occurring in $\mathrm{blocks}$, the list of transaction ids of $B$ has no duplicates (distinctness within each block only; ids may repeat across different blocks);
- $\mathrm{connectChain}(\mathrm{subsidy}, [\,], h, \mathrm{blocks}) = \text{some } u'$, i.e. connecting the blocks in order at heights $h, h+1, \dots, h+n-1$ starting from the **empty** UTXO set succeeds and yields $u'$;

**then**
$$\mathrm{tv}(u') \le \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} \mathrm{subsidy}(h + k), \qquad n = |\mathrm{blocks}|,$$
a non-strict integer inequality.

There is no explicit `keysNodup` hypothesis (the starting set is the empty list, which has no outpoints). For $\mathrm{blocks} = [\,]$ the second hypothesis forces $u' = [\,]$ and the conclusion reads $0 \le 0$. The function $\mathrm{subsidy}$ is arbitrary and may take negative values; the conclusion does not assert that the outpoints of $u'$ are distinct, nor anything about fees.

items.theorem_title: Median time past and the contextual block-header rules
items.natural_language_statement:
A chain of ancestors is the list of its block times $t_0, t_1, \dots$, most recent first. The **window** is the first $\mathrm{nMedianTimeSpan} = 11$ times. The **median time past** of a chain sorts its window by $\le$ and returns the element at index $\lfloor |w| / 2 \rfloor$, or $0$ for an empty chain:
$$\mathrm{MTP}(t_0, t_1, \dots) = \mathrm{sort}(t_0, \dots, t_{\min(10,\,n-1)})\big[\lfloor \min(11, n) / 2 \rfloor\big].$$

A **header** has a version, a time and `nBits`. $\mathrm{MAX\_FUTURE\_BLOCK\_TIME} = 7{,}200$ seconds. The mainnet activation heights are $\mathrm{BIP34Height} = 227{,}931$, $\mathrm{BIP66Height} = 363{,}725$, $\mathrm{BIP65Height} = 388{,}381$. `activeAfter`(prevHeight, h) holds when $h \le \mathrm{prevHeight} + 1$, as `DeploymentActiveAfter` for a buried deployment. `versionOutdated`(v, prevHeight) holds when $v < 2$ with BIP34 active, or $v < 3$ with BIP66 active, or $v < 4$ with BIP65 active.

`contextualCheck`(header, prevHeight, prevTimes, required, now) is `ContextualCheckBlockHeader` at mainnet parameters: `nBits` $=$ required, $\mathrm{MTP}(\text{prevTimes}) <$ time, time $\le$ now $+ 7{,}200$, and the version is not outdated. The required `nBits` is supplied by the caller, as `GetNextWorkRequired` computes it.

**Formalization Note.** Times are `Int`; the sort is `List.mergeSort` on `≤` and the index access is `getD` with default `0`. `enforce_BIP94` is `false` as on mainnet, so the testnet timewarp rule is absent. Only `Std` is imported.
items.definition:
import Std

namespace BitcoinHeader

/-! Transcription of the contextual block-header rules of Bitcoin Core at revision
`a773e1e33b349dc819b5a0edc1c7a4839dc73b48`: `CBlockIndex::GetMedianTimePast` (`chain.h`),
`ContextualCheckBlockHeader` (`validation.cpp`), `DeploymentActiveAfter` for buried deployments
(`deploymentstatus.h`), `MAX_FUTURE_BLOCK_TIME` (`chain.h`), and the mainnet activation heights
of BIP34, BIP66 and BIP65 (`kernel/chainparams.cpp`), with `enforce_BIP94 = false` as on mainnet.

A chain of ancestors is represented by the list of its block times, most recent first
(`pindex`, `pindex->pprev`, …). The required `nBits` is supplied by the caller, as it is computed
by `GetNextWorkRequired` in the proof-of-work development. -/

/-- `chain.h`: `MAX_FUTURE_BLOCK_TIME = 2 * 60 * 60`. -/
def MAX_FUTURE_BLOCK_TIME : Int := 2 * 60 * 60

/-- `CBlockIndex::nMedianTimeSpan = 11`. -/
def nMedianTimeSpan : Nat := 11

/-- `CMainParams`: `BIP34Height = 227931` (`DEPLOYMENT_HEIGHTINCB`). -/
def BIP34Height : Nat := 227931

/-- `CMainParams`: `BIP66Height = 363725` (`DEPLOYMENT_DERSIG`). -/
def BIP66Height : Nat := 363725

/-- `CMainParams`: `BIP65Height = 388381` (`DEPLOYMENT_CLTV`). -/
def BIP65Height : Nat := 388381

/-- The window `GetMedianTimePast` sorts: the times of the block and its ancestors, at most
`nMedianTimeSpan` of them. -/
def timeWindow (times : List Int) : List Int := times.take nMedianTimeSpan

/-- `GetMedianTimePast`: sort the window and take the element at index `size / 2`. The result is
`0` for an empty chain, which the source never queries. -/
def medianTimePast (times : List Int) : Int :=
  let w := timeWindow times
  (w.mergeSort fun a b => decide (a ≤ b)).getD (w.length / 2) 0

/-- A block header, reduced to the fields the contextual rules read. -/
structure Header where
  version : Int
  time : Int
  bits : BitVec 32

/-- `DeploymentActiveAfter(pindexPrev, dep)` for a buried deployment:
`pindexPrev->nHeight + 1 >= DeploymentHeight(dep)`. -/
def activeAfter (prevHeight : Nat) (deploymentHeight : Nat) : Bool :=
  decide (deploymentHeight ≤ prevHeight + 1)

/-- The version floor of `ContextualCheckBlockHeader`: rejected when the version is below 2, 3
or 4 while BIP34, BIP66 or BIP65 respectively is active for the next block. -/
def versionOutdated (version : Int) (prevHeight : Nat) : Bool :=
  (decide (version < 2) && activeAfter prevHeight BIP34Height) ||
  (decide (version < 3) && activeAfter prevHeight BIP66Height) ||
  (decide (version < 4) && activeAfter prevHeight BIP65Height)

/-- `ContextualCheckBlockHeader` at mainnet parameters: `nBits` equals the required work, the time
exceeds the previous block's median time past, the time is at most the local clock plus
`MAX_FUTURE_BLOCK_TIME`, and the version is not outdated. `prevTimes` lists the times of the
previous block and its ancestors, most recent first. -/
def contextualCheck (h : Header) (prevHeight : Nat) (prevTimes : List Int) (required : BitVec 32)
    (now : Int) : Bool :=
  decide (h.bits = required) &&
  decide (medianTimePast prevTimes < h.time) &&
  decide (h.time ≤ now + MAX_FUTURE_BLOCK_TIME) &&
  !versionOutdated h.version prevHeight

end BitcoinHeader

items.readback:
**`MAX_FUTURE_BLOCK_TIME`.** This is a named integer constant (an element of $\mathbb{Z}$, not of $\mathbb{N}$) whose value is $2 \cdot 60 \cdot 60 = 7200$. Nothing else is asserted about it; it is simply the number $7200$ typed as an integer.

**`nMedianTimeSpan`.** This is a named natural-number constant whose value is $11$.

**`BIP34Height`.** This is a named natural-number constant whose value is $227931$.

**`BIP66Height`.** This is a named natural-number constant whose value is $363725$.

**`BIP65Height`.** This is a named natural-number constant whose value is $388381$.

**`timeWindow`.** This is a function from finite lists of integers to finite lists of integers. Given a list $T = [t_0, t_1, t_2, \dots]$ of integers (indexed from $0$, in the order in which the list is given), $\mathrm{timeWindow}(T)$ is the list consisting of the first $\min(11, |T|)$ entries of $T$, in their original order:
$$\mathrm{timeWindow}(T) = [t_0, t_1, \dots, t_{\min(11,|T|)-1}].$$
If $|T| \le 11$ the window is $T$ itself (in particular, the window of the empty list is the empty list); if $|T| > 11$ the entries $t_{11}, t_{12}, \dots$ are discarded. No sorting or reordering takes place in this definition.

**`medianTimePast`.** This is a function from finite lists of integers to a single integer. Given a list of integers $T$, let $W = \mathrm{timeWindow}(T)$ be the list of its first $\min(11,|T|)$ entries as above, let $n = |W|$ (so $0 \le n \le 11$), and let $W^{\uparrow} = [w_0 \le w_1 \le \dots \le w_{n-1}]$ be the list obtained by sorting $W$ into non-decreasing order (a merge sort using the comparison "$a \le b$"; since equal integers are indistinguishable as values, the handling of ties does not affect the result). Then
$$\mathrm{medianTimePast}(T) = \begin{cases} w_{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor} & \text{if } n \ge 1,\\ 0 & \text{if } n = 0,\end{cases}$$
where $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ is natural-number division (rounding down) and indexing is from $0$. Concretely: the function reads the entry at position $\lfloor n/2 \rfloor$ of the sorted window and returns the fallback value $0$ if that position does not exist, which happens exactly when the window is empty, i.e. exactly when $T$ is the empty list. For $n \ge 1$ the position $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ always lies in range, so the fallback is never used. When $n$ is odd, say $n = 2k+1$, the result is $w_k$, the unique middle element of the sorted window (the $(k+1)$-st smallest). When $n$ is even and positive, say $n = 2k$, the result is $w_k$, the *upper* of the two middle elements (the $(k+1)$-st smallest), not their average and not the lower middle element. For example, for $T = [a]$ the result is $a$; for $T = [a, b]$ the result is $\max(a,b)$; for $T$ of length $\ge 11$ the result is $w_5$, the $6$-th smallest among the first $11$ entries of $T$. Note that the result is always a value that occurs in the window when $T \ne []$, and is the number $0$ (which need not occur in $T$) when $T = []$.

**`Header`.** This is a record type with exactly three fields and no constraints between them: a field `version`, which is an arbitrary integer (it may be negative or arbitrarily large; it is not restricted to 32 bits); a field `time`, which is an arbitrary integer (likewise unrestricted); and a field `bits`, which is a bit-vector of exactly $32$ bits (equivalently, an element of $\{0, 1, \dots, 2^{32}-1\}$). Any triple of such values is a `Header`.

**`activeAfter`.** This is a function taking two natural numbers, $p$ (named `prevHeight`) and $d$ (named `deploymentHeight`), and returning a Boolean truth value (`true`/`false`). It returns `true` exactly when
$$d \le p + 1,$$
where $+$ is natural-number addition (no overflow), and `false` otherwise. Equivalently, it is `true` iff $p \ge d - 1$ when $d \ge 1$, and is always `true` when $d = 0$.

**`versionOutdated`.** This is a function taking an integer $v$ (named `version`; any integer, possibly negative) and a natural number $p$ (named `prevHeight`) and returning a Boolean. It is `true` exactly when at least one of the following three conditions holds (Boolean "or" of three Boolean "and"s):
$$\bigl(v < 2 \;\wedge\; 227931 \le p+1\bigr) \;\vee\; \bigl(v < 3 \;\wedge\; 363725 \le p+1\bigr) \;\vee\; \bigl(v < 4 \;\wedge\; 388381 \le p+1\bigr),$$
where each "$d \le p + 1$" is the `activeAfter` test unfolded with $d$ equal to the constants $227931$, $363725$, $388381$ respectively. Here $v < 2$ etc. are integer comparisons (so, e.g., every negative $v$ satisfies all three), and $p + 1$ is natural-number addition. Equivalently (since $227931 \le p+1 \iff p \ge 227930$, etc.): `true` iff ($v \le 1$ and $p \ge 227930$) or ($v \le 2$ and $p \ge 363724$) or ($v \le 3$ and $p \ge 388380$). For $p \le 227929$ the function is `false` regardless of $v$; for $v \ge 4$ the function is `false` regardless of $p$.

**`contextualCheck`.** This is a function taking a `Header` $h$ (with integer fields $h.\mathrm{version}$, $h.\mathrm{time}$ and 32-bit field $h.\mathrm{bits}$), a natural number $p$ (named `prevHeight`), a list of integers $P$ (named `prevTimes`), a 32-bit bit-vector $r$ (named `required`, supplied by the caller and not computed by anything in this file), and an integer $\nu$ (named `now`; an arbitrary integer parameter), and returning a Boolean. It is `true` exactly when all four of the following hold (Boolean "and" of four conditions):

1. $h.\mathrm{bits} = r$, equality of 32-bit bit-vectors;
2. $\mathrm{medianTimePast}(P) < h.\mathrm{time}$ (strict), where $\mathrm{medianTimePast}(P)$ is, as unfolded above, the entry at position $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ of the non-decreasing sort of the first $n=\min(11,|P|)$ entries of $P$, and is $0$ when $P$ is the empty list — so for $P = []$ this conjunct reads $0 < h.\mathrm{time}$;
3. $h.\mathrm{time} \le \nu + 7200$ (non-strict), integer arithmetic, where $7200$ is the constant `MAX_FUTURE_BLOCK_TIME`;
4. the Boolean negation of $\mathrm{versionOutdated}(h.\mathrm{version}, p)$, i.e.
$$\neg\Bigl[\bigl(h.\mathrm{version} < 2 \wedge 227931 \le p+1\bigr) \vee \bigl(h.\mathrm{version} < 3 \wedge 363725 \le p+1\bigr) \vee \bigl(h.\mathrm{version} < 4 \wedge 388381 \le p+1\bigr)\Bigr].$$

It is `false` if any one of the four conditions fails. Nothing in this definition relates $p$ to $|P|$, relates $\nu$ to the entries of $P$, or constrains $r$ in any way; all five inputs are independent.

items.theorem_title: The median time past lies within any bounds of the window
items.formal_statement:
theorem BitcoinHeader.mtp_bounds (times : List Int) (h : times ≠ []) (lo hi : Int)
    (hb : ∀ t ∈ BitcoinHeader.timeWindow times, lo ≤ t ∧ t ≤ hi) :
    lo ≤ BitcoinHeader.medianTimePast times ∧ BitcoinHeader.medianTimePast times ≤ hi := by sorry
items.natural_language_statement: For every non-empty chain and integers $lo \le hi$ such that every time $t$ in the window satisfies $lo \le t \le hi$, also $lo \le \mathrm{MTP}(\text{times}) \le hi$. In particular the median is between the oldest and the newest time of the window.

    BitcoinHeader.medianTimePast times ≤ BitcoinHeader.medianTimePast (t :: times) := by sorry

items.theorem_title: The outdated-version condition as height thresholds
items.formal_statement:
theorem BitcoinHeader.versionOutdated_iff (version : Int) (prevHeight : Nat) :
    BitcoinHeader.versionOutdated version prevHeight = true ↔
      (version < 2 ∧ BitcoinHeader.BIP34Height ≤ prevHeight + 1) ∨
      (version < 3 ∧ BitcoinHeader.BIP66Height ≤ prevHeight + 1) ∨
      (version < 4 ∧ BitcoinHeader.BIP65Height ≤ prevHeight + 1) := by sorry
items.natural_language_statement:

$$(v < 2 \wedge 227{,}931 \le p + 1) \;\vee\; (v < 3 \wedge 363{,}725 \le p + 1) \;\vee\; (v < 4 \wedge 388{,}381 \le p + 1),$$
the BIP34, BIP66 and BIP65 version floors at their mainnet activation heights.

items.theorem_title: Acceptance by the contextual header check, characterized
items.formal_statement:
theorem BitcoinHeader.contextualCheck_iff (h : BitcoinHeader.Header) (prevHeight : Nat) (prevTimes : List Int)
    (required : BitVec 32) (now : Int) :
    BitcoinHeader.contextualCheck h prevHeight prevTimes required now = true ↔
      h.bits = required ∧
      BitcoinHeader.medianTimePast prevTimes < h.time ∧
      h.time ≤ now + BitcoinHeader.MAX_FUTURE_BLOCK_TIME ∧
      ¬ ((h.version < 2 ∧ BitcoinHeader.BIP34Height ≤ prevHeight + 1) ∨
         (h.version < 3 ∧ BitcoinHeader.BIP66Height ≤ prevHeight + 1) ∨
         (h.version < 4 ∧ BitcoinHeader.BIP65Height ≤ prevHeight + 1)) := by sorry
items.natural_language_statement:
For every header $h$, previous height $p$, chain of previous times, required `nBits` $r$ and local time $now$, the contextual check accepts exactly when
$$h.\mathrm{bits} = r \;\wedge\; \mathrm{MTP}(\text{prevTimes}) < h.\mathrm{time} \;\wedge\; h.\mathrm{time} \le now + 7{,}200 \;\wedge\; \neg\,\mathrm{outdated},$$
where outdated is the disjunction of the three version-floor conditions. These are the `bad-diffbits`, `time-too-old`, `time-too-new` and `bad-version` rejections of `ContextualCheckBlockHeader`.

items.theorem_title: Median time past is non-decreasing along a chain obeying time-too-old
items.formal_statement:
theorem BitcoinHeader.mtp_mono_chain (times : List Int)
    (hok : ∀ (i : Nat) (hi : i < times.length),
      BitcoinHeader.medianTimePast (times.drop (i + 1)) < times[i]) :
    ∀ (i j : Nat), i ≤ j → j ≤ times.length →
      BitcoinHeader.medianTimePast (times.drop j) ≤ BitcoinHeader.medianTimePast (times.drop i) := by sorry
items.natural_language_statement:
Let $t_0, t_1, \dots, t_{n-1}$ be the block times of a chain, most recent first, such that every block satisfies the `time-too-old` rule against its predecessor:
$$\forall i < n,\quad \mathrm{MTP}(t_{i+1}, t_{i+2}, \dots) < t_i .$$
Then for all $i \le j \le n$,
$$\mathrm{MTP}(t_j, t_{j+1}, \dots) \le \mathrm{MTP}(t_i, t_{i+1}, \dots):$$
the median time past of any ancestor is at most that of any descendant. Here $\mathrm{MTP}$ is the transcription of `GetMedianTimePast`: the element at index $\lfloor |w|/2 \rfloor$ of the sorted window of at most eleven most recent times.

This is the clock-monotonicity property that time-based lock-times (BIP113, BIP68) rely on: once the chain's median time has passed a threshold, it never falls back below it. The chain's times themselves need not be increasing; only the median rule is assumed.

**Formalization Note.** The statement is about suffixes `times.drop i` of the time list; the hypothesis is the `time-too-old` conjunct of `ContextualCheckBlockHeader` at every position.

items.theorem_title: Buried deployments, script-verification flags by height, and the two exception blocks
items.natural_language_statement:
A **buried deployment** is one of `HEIGHTINCB` (BIP34), `CLTV` (BIP65), `DERSIG` (BIP66), `CSV`, `SEGWIT`, with mainnet activation heights $227{,}931$, $388{,}381$, $363{,}725$, $419{,}328$, $481{,}824$ (`deploymentHeight`). `activeAt`(height, dep) holds when the deployment height is at most the block height, as `DeploymentActiveAt`; `activeAfter`(prevHeight, dep) holds when it is at most prevHeight $+ 1$, as `DeploymentActiveAfter`.

A **flag set** is a record of seven Booleans: `p2sh`, `witness`, `taproot`, `dersig`, `cltv`, `csv`, `nulldummy`. `noFlags` has none; `baseFlags` has `p2sh`, `witness`, `taproot`. A block's **exception status** is `none`, `bip16Block` (the hash-keyed P2SH violation) or `taprootBlock` (the hash-keyed Taproot violation); `exceptionBase` yields `baseFlags`, `noFlags`, and `p2sh`+`witness` respectively.

`blockScriptFlags`(height, exc) is `GetBlockScriptFlags`: the exception base, with `dersig`, `cltv`, `csv`, `nulldummy` each OR-ed with `activeAt` of `DERSIG`, `CLTV`, `CSV`, `SEGWIT` at the height. `ScriptFlags.le` is pointwise inclusion: every flag true in the first is true in the second.

$\mathrm{LOCKTIME\_VERIFY\_SEQUENCE} = 1$, and `lockTimeFlags`(height) is that value when `CSV` is active at the height and $0$ otherwise, as `nLockTimeFlags` in `ConnectBlock`.

**Formalization Note.** The exception table is modeled by the three-valued classification rather than a hash lookup. Versionbits deployments are not modeled, since the pinned source consults none for mainnet consensus flags. Only `Std` is imported.
items.definition:
import Std

namespace BitcoinActivation

/-! Transcription of the historical rule selection of Bitcoin Core at revision
`a773e1e33b349dc819b5a0edc1c7a4839dc73b48`: the buried deployment heights of `CMainParams`
(`kernel/chainparams.cpp`), `DeploymentActiveAt` / `DeploymentActiveAfter` for buried deployments
(`deploymentstatus.h`), `GetBlockScriptFlags` with the two `script_flag_exceptions`
(`validation.cpp`), and the `nLockTimeFlags` selection in `ConnectBlock`. -/

/-- `Consensus::BuriedDeployment`. -/
inductive BuriedDeployment where
  | heightInCB   -- BIP34
  | cltv         -- BIP65
  | derSig       -- BIP66
  | csv          -- BIP68/112/113
  | segwit       -- BIP141/143/147
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- `Consensus::Params::DeploymentHeight` at mainnet values. -/
def deploymentHeight : BuriedDeployment → Nat
  | .heightInCB => 227931
  | .cltv => 388381
  | .derSig => 363725
  | .csv => 419328
  | .segwit => 481824

/-- `DeploymentActiveAt(index, dep) = index.nHeight >= DeploymentHeight(dep)`. -/
def activeAt (height : Nat) (dep : BuriedDeployment) : Bool := decide (deploymentHeight dep ≤ height)

/-- `DeploymentActiveAfter(pindexPrev, dep) = pindexPrev->nHeight + 1 >= DeploymentHeight(dep)`. -/
def activeAfter (prevHeight : Nat) (dep : BuriedDeployment) : Bool :=
  decide (deploymentHeight dep ≤ prevHeight + 1)

/-- The consensus script-verification flags `GetBlockScriptFlags` can set. -/
structure ScriptFlags where
  p2sh : Bool
  witness : Bool
  taproot : Bool
  dersig : Bool
  cltv : Bool
  csv : Bool
  nulldummy : Bool
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- `SCRIPT_VERIFY_NONE`. -/
def noFlags : ScriptFlags := ⟨false, false, false, false, false, false, false⟩

/-- The default base `SCRIPT_VERIFY_P2SH | SCRIPT_VERIFY_WITNESS | SCRIPT_VERIFY_TAPROOT`. -/
def baseFlags : ScriptFlags := ⟨true, true, true, false, false, false, false⟩

/-- `consensus.script_flag_exceptions`: the block is one of the two historical exceptions, or
not. The BIP16 exception (`00000000000002dc…9c22`) maps to `SCRIPT_VERIFY_NONE`; the Taproot
exception (`0000000000000000000f14c3…95ad`) maps to `SCRIPT_VERIFY_P2SH | SCRIPT_VERIFY_WITNESS`. -/
inductive ScriptException where
  | none
  | bip16Block
  | taprootBlock
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- The flags the exception table yields, or the default base. -/
def exceptionBase : ScriptException → ScriptFlags
  | .none => baseFlags
  | .bip16Block => noFlags
  | .taprootBlock => ⟨true, true, false, false, false, false, false⟩

/-- `GetBlockScriptFlags(block_index)` at mainnet: the base (default or exception), then
`DERSIG`, `CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY`, `CHECKSEQUENCEVERIFY` and `NULLDUMMY` added when BIP66, BIP65,
CSV and SegWit respectively are active at the block's height. -/
def blockScriptFlags (height : Nat) (exc : ScriptException) : ScriptFlags :=
  let f := exceptionBase exc
  { f with
    dersig := f.dersig || activeAt height .derSig
    cltv := f.cltv || activeAt height .cltv
    csv := f.csv || activeAt height .csv
    nulldummy := f.nulldummy || activeAt height .segwit }

/-- Pointwise inclusion of flag sets: every rule enforced by the first is enforced by the second. -/
def ScriptFlags.le (a b : ScriptFlags) : Prop :=
  (a.p2sh = true → b.p2sh = true) ∧ (a.witness = true → b.witness = true) ∧
  (a.taproot = true → b.taproot = true) ∧ (a.dersig = true → b.dersig = true) ∧
  (a.cltv = true → b.cltv = true) ∧ (a.csv = true → b.csv = true) ∧
  (a.nulldummy = true → b.nulldummy = true)

/-- `consensus/consensus.h`: `LOCKTIME_VERIFY_SEQUENCE = (1 << 0)`. -/
def LOCKTIME_VERIFY_SEQUENCE : Nat := 1

/-- The `nLockTimeFlags` of `ConnectBlock`: `LOCKTIME_VERIFY_SEQUENCE` once CSV is active at the
block's height, else `0`. -/
def lockTimeFlags (height : Nat) : Nat :=
  if activeAt height .csv then LOCKTIME_VERIFY_SEQUENCE else 0

end BitcoinActivation

The comments next to the constructors mention BIP numbers, but those comments carry no formal content: an element of this type is just one of five labels.

**`deploymentHeight`** (function $\mathsf{deploymentHeight} : \mathsf{BuriedDeployment} \to \mathbb{N}$). A total function from the five labels to natural numbers, given by the table

\begin{aligned}
\mathsf{deploymentHeight}(\mathsf{heightInCB}) &= 227931,\\
\mathsf{deploymentHeight}(\mathsf{cltv}) &= 388381,\\
\mathsf{deploymentHeight}(\mathsf{derSig}) &= 363725,\\
\mathsf{deploymentHeight}(\mathsf{csv}) &= 419328,\\
\mathsf{deploymentHeight}(\mathsf{segwit}) &= 481824.
\end{aligned}
$$

Note that the numeric order of these values ($227931 < 363725 < 388381 < 419328 < 481824$) is not the order in which the constructors are listed: $\mathsf{derSig}$ ($363725$) is numerically below $\mathsf{cltv}$ ($388381$) although $\mathsf{cltv}$ is listed first.

For a natural number $h$ ("height") and a label $d$, $\mathsf{activeAt}(h, d)$ is the *Boolean value* (not a proposition) that is $\mathsf{true}$ exactly when $\mathsf{deploymentHeight}(d) \le h$ and $\mathsf{false}$ otherwise. In particular the comparison is non-strict: at $h = \mathsf{deploymentHeight}(d)$ itself the value is $\mathsf{true}$. Heights are natural numbers, so $h = 0$ is allowed (giving $\mathsf{false}$ for every label, since every tabulated height is positive) and no negative height exists.

For a natural number $p$ ("previous height") and a label $d$, $\mathsf{activeAfter}(p, d)$ is the Boolean value that is $\mathsf{true}$ exactly when $\mathsf{deploymentHeight}(d) \le p + 1$, and $\mathsf{false}$ otherwise. A record with exactly seven Boolean fields, in this order: $\mathsf{p2sh}$, $\mathsf{witness}$, $\mathsf{taproot}$, $\mathsf{dersig}$, $\mathsf{cltv}$, $\mathsf{csv}$, $\mathsf{nulldummy}$. A byte is an 8-bit word; a stack element is a list of bytes. Limits: element size $520$, $201$ operations, $20$ keys per multisig, $1000$ stack elements, $4$-byte numbers.

**Numbers.** $\mathrm{leNat}$ is the little-endian value of a byte list; $\mathrm{topBit}$ is bit 7 of the last byte; $\mathrm{clearTop}$ clears it; $\mathrm{setVch}(v)$ is `CScriptNum::set_vch`: $-\mathrm{leNat}(\mathrm{clearTop}\,v)$ when the top bit is set, else $\mathrm{leNat}(v)$, and $0$ for the empty list. $\mathrm{natBytes}(n)$ is the little-endian byte loop without trailing zeros; $\mathrm{setTop}$ sets bit 7 of the last byte; $\mathrm{serialize}(n)$ is `CScriptNum::serialize`: empty for $0$, else the magnitude bytes with a sign byte `0x80`/`0x00` appended when their top bit is already set, or the top bit set for a negative value otherwise. $\mathrm{nonMinimal}(v)$ is the constructor's rejection test (last byte has no value bits and the previous byte does not need it); $\mathrm{toNum}(\text{requireMinimal}, \text{maxSize}, v)$ is the constructor, `none` where it throws. $\mathrm{castToBool}$ is `CastToBool`; `vchTrue` $= [1]$, `vchFalse` $= [\,]$.

**Scripts.** An instruction is a data push or a non-push opcode byte; a script is a list of instructions, the output of `GetOp`. Opcode constants follow `script.h`; `isDisabled` lists the fifteen CVE-2010-5137 opcodes.

**Flags and oracle.** `Flags` holds `CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY`, `CHECKSEQUENCEVERIFY`, `NULLDUMMY`. An `Oracle` supplies `ripemd160`, `sha1`, `sha256`, `hash160`, `hash256`, `checkSig` (returning `none` where an encoding check fails the script, `some b` for the signature verdict), `checkLockTime` and `checkSequence`.

**Execution.** A `State` is the main stack, alt stack, condition stack and `nOpCount`, stacks top-first. `execOp`(flags, oracle, fExec, opcode, state) is the `switch` of `EvalScript` for one opcode: small-integer pushes, `NOP`s, `CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY`/`CHECKSEQUENCEVERIFY` (5-byte numbers, negative rejected, disable flag), `IF`/`NOTIF`/`ELSE`/`ENDIF`, `VERIFY`, `RETURN`, the stack family (`TOALTSTACK` … `TUCK`, `SIZE`), `EQUAL`/`EQUALVERIFY`, the unary and binary numeric family on 4-byte operands, `WITHIN`, the five hash opcodes, `CODESEPARATOR`, `CHECKSIG`/`CHECKSIGVERIFY`, `CHECKMULTISIG`/`CHECKMULTISIGVERIFY` with key-count accounting, the `NULLDUMMY` test and the extra popped element; anything else is a bad opcode. `step` is one loop iteration: element-size check and conditional push for a push; for an opcode, the `nOpCount` increment and $201$ test (only for opcodes above `OP_16`: `OP_1NEGATE`, `OP_RESERVED` and `OP_1`…`OP_16` are not counted, as in the source), the disabled test, execute-or-skip, and the stack-size check. `run` is the loop plus the final unbalanced-conditional check; `evalScript` returns the main stack; `verifyScriptPlain` is `VerifyScript` for a `scriptPubKey` that is neither P2SH nor a witness program. `p2pkhScript` and `p2pkScript` are the two templates; `opsIn` counts the instructions `nOpCount` counts: non-push opcodes above `OP_16`.

**Formalization Note.** `SigVersion::BASE` only; `fRequireMinimal` false; policy flags off; byte-level parsing, `MAX_SCRIPT_SIZE`, P2SH, witness programs and Tapscript are out of scope. An `op` instruction is meant for the bytes `GetOp` returns as non-push opcodes (above `OP_PUSHDATA4`); a push-range byte used as `op` behaves like an unknown opcode. Only `Std` is imported.
